ResponsesInList.Title: Collapsed topics 405.1.2
ResponsesInList.Text: At our school, we are fans of the 'collapsed topics' course format. We appreciate the clear section indicators and the ability to highlight sections for students. Recently, we upgraded to Moodle 4.5 (now: 4.5.6 build 20250811) and are using version 405.1.2 of collapsed topics (released July 6th 2025). There are subsections, but these are not collapsible. When working with a section that has access restrictions, the section becomes invisible to students. We would like the access restrictions (e.g., "not available unless...") to be visible to students, just as they are for teachers. Would it be possible to program this?

ResponsesInList.Title: Grid Format v405.1.5 on Moodle v4.5.6: Restricted Subsections Affecting Course Index Display
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, all. I hope you're all having good starts to your respective weeks. We've encountered a small issue with format_grid v405.1.5. Our Moodle site is currently running on v4.5.6. When a course is in the 'Grid' format, any subsections that are restricted, but not hidden, prevent students' 'Course Index' from loading. For an example of this issue, please see the screenshot below, taken from a student persona. The two subsections being restricted, and currently unavailable, prevent the 'Course Index' (on the left of the screenshot) from loading. This issue only affects users without the permission to bypass activity restrictions. It's caused by all 'Restrict access' types ('Group', 'Date', etc.) where the content is restricted, and thus unavailable, but not hidden. Restricted subsections don't cause this issue for other course formats. Please could this behaviour be patched in future updates to the Grid format plugin? Many thanks. All the best, Tom

ResponsesInList.Title: New Popup activities format release
ResponsesInList.Text: The Popup activities course format has been updated. The current version 1.0.22 has support for more activity types. Recent additions include Content designer , Plenary meeting , and External tool . Some bugs have also been fixed. The format behaves similarly to Custom sections format (topics) except that supported activities are opened in a modal rather that opening a new page. The format has an optional integration with the Deft response block that allows teacher to update course page and to have the changes appear remotely on the students course page. Completion changes are also reflected immediately. Future plans include add more audio and video integration.

ResponsesInList.Title: New Popup activities format release
ResponsesInList.Text: Version 1.0.23 has been released which has some improvement in the way that it reacts to editing when integrated with the Deft response block. The course page will now react when an editing teacher moves activities. Students should see all visible changes to the course as the teacher makes them when updating is enabled. There is also a new release of Deft response 1.3 that now allows embedding a conference venue within the block on the course page. This allows the teacher to talk with students on a course page while they engage in the activities on the page. The teacher can change which activities are visible to students in a similar way that polls are used in a webinar application.

ResponsesInList.Title: Course dashboard: Change number of courses from 12 to 24
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I am looking at the myoverview page at `example.com/my/` It's the block with the `id="block-myoverview-xxxxxxxxxxxxx"` that displays a list or card list of courses. Below the cards display there is the paging dropdown where I can switch between "12" and "all" list items or cards. I'd like to change the default from 12 to 24 items, but was not able to find the config value for this. The list is called & populated with this request, and it always pulls 12 items from the database , even if I put limit = 24 to the POST data: `https://example.com/lib/ajax/service.php?sesskey=xxxxxx&info=core_course_get_enrolled_courses_by_timeline_classification` `POST: [{"index":0,"methodname":"core_course_get_enrolled_courses_by_timeline_classification","args":{"offset":0,"limit":24,"classification":"allincludinghidden","sort":"fullname","customfieldname":"","customfieldvalue":"","requiredfields":["id","fullname","shortname","showcoursecategory","showshortname","visible","enddate","summary","summaryformat"]}}]` There is a Mustache marker in the file `/lib/templates/paged_content_paging_bar.mustache` that is called `itemsperpage` , but I cannot find a place where I can set a default for that value. Can you help me out?

ResponsesInList.Title: Course dashboard: Change number of courses from 12 to 24
ResponsesInList.Text: Dear Mateng, In 'blocks/myoverview/classes/output/main.php', change: `$this->paging = $paging ? $paging : BLOCK_MYOVERVIEW_PAGING_12;` to: `$this->paging = $paging ? $paging : BLOCK_MYOVERVIEW_PAGING_24;` Kind regards, Gareth

ResponsesInList.Title: Course dashboard: Change number of courses from 12 to 24
ResponsesInList.Text: Dear Gareth, thanks for the reply. I am now actually getting a larger array (all 15 courses) from the ajax request, however the display is still is paginated into pages of 12 items each. I still see the dropdown "paging-control-limit-container-1" with the options 12 and all . Edit: I found the constant NUMCOURSES_PERPAGE in the file /blocks/myoverview/amd/build/view.min.js (blocks/myoverview/amd/src/view.js) After deleting all caches and JavaScript caches it finally worked. I have 15 courses on my local instance and they are all displayed. 🥳 I guess when I have > 25 courses in the database, the pagination will be shown again with option 24 / all. Now I have to find a method to make this change applicable after each update. Edit 2: I reverted my changes in main.php, tested it and it still works. So it's enough to modify NUMCOURSES_PERPAGE in the JS file.

ResponsesInList.Title: Course dashboard: Change number of courses from 12 to 24
ResponsesInList.Text: Dear Mateng, Are you changing NUMCOURSES_PERPAGE (which is an array) to remove the '12' element?  If so then 'NUMCOURSES_PERPAGE' is used to provide options to the user and the 'active' select in the dropdown is determined by 'pagingLimit' in the 'itemsPerPageFunc' function in the same 'view.js' file.  'pagingLimit' is populated by a 'data' attribute on a tag that's populated by the code in main.php outlined.  The reason that a given user may not have '24' selected after the code has changed is because its a user preference (thus when testing remove the relevant user preference for the test user (I forget off the top of my head which one but it should be obvious.... look in the block's lib.php file too)).  Therefore to give the user the ability to set '12' if they want, whilst at the same time have '24' as the initial default is the solution I proposed.  If it is desired that core code does not change then it's likely to be possible to override 'main.php' in a theme as it appears to be autoloaded. Kind regards, Gareth

ResponsesInList.Title: Course dashboard: Change number of courses from 12 to 24
ResponsesInList.Text: > Are you changing NUMCOURSES_PERPAGE (which is an array) to remove the '12' element? That's true, that was exactly my change that finally worked. I know it's a dirty hack and I will be immensely grateful if I can learn how to avoid stuff like that. > The reason that a given user may not have '24' selected after the code has changed is because its a user preference Now I understand. How can we remove all user settings in a case like this, so everybody will see our new defaults?

ResponsesInList.Title: Course dashboard: Change number of courses from 12 to 24
ResponsesInList.Text: Dear Mateng, It will be the 'block_myoverview_user_paging_preference' ( https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/MOODLE_500_STABLE/blocks/myoverview/lib.php#L139-L151 ) entries in the 'user_preferences' table in the database.  Not sure how to clear via the UI, but there might be a way with the privacy stuff.  As always when messing with the database, have a backup! Kind regards, Gareth

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Flexible Course Format
ResponsesInList.Text: Dear Joanna, The current last supported version is 3.6.1 (Build: 20181205) -> https://bitbucket.org/covuni/moodle-format_flexible/src/773bd6fadcf4682f3cf6fff361044e7ffd468bf0/version.php#lines-35 . Since then the course format API has been changed drastically and therefore won't (I extremely suspect) work on Moodle 4.5. Flexible was developed from the Grid format by me (funded) as you can see here: https://bitbucket.org/covuni/moodle-format_flexible/commits/branch/master . To make Grid work with the changed course format API, I needed to rebuild it from scratch. This was not trivial. However, the only ways I can see technically to bring Flexible forward would be to repeat the same process from the current Grid format, or replicate what Grid currently does not have that Flexible does. If I were to do this (the later), then again, my time would have to be funded.  For the former would depend on what 'Jez H' would like to do with the format and take things from there. Kind regards, Gareth

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Flexible Course Format
ResponsesInList.Text: Dear Joanna, As I mentioned, themes and course format are two completely different types of plugin. To advise you on what to do I'd need to understand your specific requirements. My time for such would have to be funded. You could install both on a test server , look at what documentation is out there and then see what they do. With Adaptable extra functionality for sponsors, that is subject to change and can be understood for a specific version by what has been indicated as not available in the theme settings (italic text / disabled).  There is guidance that I issue when contacted directly when you're using the theme. If you wanted me to 'revive' the Flexible format then the time scale depends on my workload and what I may encounter along the way, as it's bespoke development - normally a certain amount of hours spread out over days etc.  Cost wise, certainly a three figure sum in GBP, possibly a low four figure sum.  With "And would you advise going this route for someone with little support.....locally." then I advise to seek out and get local support. ResponsesInList.Title: Disappointed in subsections

Course format is grid When the course copy completed, section 0 was repeated four times. Has anyone got an idea what might have happpened? Release 401.2.3, version 2022112609 on Moodle 4.1.13 (Build: 20240902).

Did the manager think that the copy kept failing, then repeated the process with the 'merge' option? Kind regards, Gareth

ResponsesInList.Title: Sections being duplicated in course restore

ResponsesInList.Title: Collapsed Topics release candidate version V500.0.1 for Moodle 5.0 released
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello, I've released the release candidate version of the Collapsed Topics course format for Moodle 5.0 as follows: Release 500.0.1 for Moodle 5.0 version 2025041400.00 (Build: 20250414) and above within the MOODLE_500_STABLE branch: https://moodle.org/plugins/format_topcoll/500.0.1/35794 https://github.com/gjbarnard/moodle-format_topcoll/releases/tag/V500.0.1 with: First Moodle 5.0 version. Update section highlight in line with core changes. Plus from the V405.1.0: Fix 'ARIA attribute for accessibility : aria-labelledby' - #160. Fix keyboard control of toggles in terms of focussing only on a the actual element that does the toggling. Fix 'Space key input not registered with the system Inplace editable in sections titles' - #161. Fix 'defaulttogglepersistence' not working. Improve single section page logic, especially when returning to course from creating a module. Important: Because of 'Subsection support' which has been incredibly difficult to support to the extent that I've had to wave a 'white flag' and remove the 'numsections' setting.  The course format API has been broken apart into so many interconnected small pieces (each tending to have separate PHP, JS and Mustache files), https://moodledev.io/docs/4.5/apis/plugintypes/format#format-output-classes-and-templates and https://moodledev.io/docs/4.5/apis/plugintypes/format#the-course-editor-structure , that it is difficult at times to understand and keep in working memory what is going on and where a given element of functionality is implemented to the extent where it can be overridden and changed.  Thus the format will now operate as 'Topics' does in terms of number of sections management.  Collapsed Topics was only ever designed to operate on sections and as such sees sub-sections as different entities not related to the number of sections in a course.  Collapsed Topics will now not allow you to have as many 'Sub sections' as you want - as was in V405.0.2 - due to increased chance of course restore failure, see: MDL-84874 .  Additional tracker issues of interest for this are: MDL-84038 and MDL-84291 . Because of the removal of 'numsections', this has an impact on backup and restore, which I've tested.  However with such a change brings risk and a greater chance of error, thus I cannot stress enough that you MUST test and be sure that the format works as expected before it goes anywhere near a production server .  I found with the Grid format that once 'numsections' was removed that it was tricky to go back, and therefore it would be unlikely even with the flexibility I like of being able to set the number of sections both as a course setting and add / remove in the course itself. I have refactored the whole toggle state preference JavaScript such that it no longer uses YUI.  This I hope will help to keep the format going for many years to come as older technologies are removed from core. Note: Always install on a test server to confirm that the format does what you want it to do before updating or installing on a production server!  And as this release could contain bugs and so I strongly recommend that you check on a test server first!  Not sure how to set one up?  Then look at the 'Installer packages' on https://download.moodle.org/releases/latest/ . Ensure that you have multiple backups of all data before using.  Please report any issues. i.e. 'bugs' with this release ONLY here.  Before doing so please read 'Reporting issues' on the 'Information' tab on the course format 'Settings' under 'Site administration' -> 'Plugins' -> 'Course formats' -> 'Collapsed Topics'. If you find this post useful, then please mark it so. Thank you, Gareth

Note: Always install on a test server to confirm that the format does what you want it to do before updating or installing on a production server!  And as this release could contain bugs and so I strongly recommend that you check on a test server first!  Not sure how to set one up?  Then look at the 'Installer packages' on https://download.moodle.org/releases/latest/ . Ensure that you have multiple backups of all data before using.  Please report any issues. i.e. 'bugs' with this release ONLY here.  Before doing so please read 'Reporting issues' on the 'Information' tab on the course format 'Settings' under 'Site administration' -> 'Plugins' -> 'Course formats' -> 'Collapsed Topics'. If you find this post useful, then please mark it so. Thank you, Gareth

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Collapsed Topics updated from V405.0.1 to V405.0.2 for Moodle 4.5
ResponsesInList.Text: Looks like this can happen in 'Custom sections' too, please see MDL-84874 . It did take me a while to deduce the replication steps, thus I welcome peer replication of the steps + any comments you may have, positive or negative. I believe that not implementing MDL-83056 is a mistake and so is MDL-84291 . Sub-sections are not 'sections' they are modules that contain other modules. If they were 'sections' then you'd be able to move a 'sub-section' to become a 'section' and vice-versa. Please also see: https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=464693 .

ResponsesInList.Title: wish: Design custom sections more accessible with closed sections
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello, We want to work more with Moodle Core settings. The standard theme ‘custom sections ’ has evolved nicely. However, one little thing would be very helpful for accessibility . Is it possible to add a function that allows you to optionally select in the settings that the theme sections are collapsed when the course is opened? If you work with a screen reader or navigate using the keyboard, you unfortunately have to click along very long paths. The table of contents is also difficult to navigate. It would therefore be very helpful for many people (including sighted people) if they could get an overview of the sections in the main course section as soon as they open the course. I have added a screenshot to show the desired initial state when opening a course. https://moodle.org/pluginfile.php/155/mod_forum/post/1874483/Course%20Entry%20Screen.JPG Kind regards, Julia

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: wish: Design custom sections more accessible with closed sections
ResponsesInList.Text: Dear Julia, 'Custom sections' is a course format, not a theme. So I'll moved the post to the 'Courses and course format's' forum. Kind regards, Gareth Moderator

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: wish: Design custom sections more accessible with closed sections
ResponsesInList.Text: Dear Julia, Possible but there would have to be an improvement to the core code for this to happen.  Or the format could be cloned into another one and the changes made to that. My Collapsed Topics format does support this already if the toggle state is not stored (shown as 'On' here): Kind regards, Gareth

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: wish: Design custom sections more accessible with closed sections
ResponsesInList.Text: Hallo Gareth, thanks for moving my thread to the right forum! We really like using your collapsed theme!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: wish: Design custom sections more accessible with closed sections
ResponsesInList.Text: Dear Julia, No problem. My Collapsed Topics format has a function whereby you can click on an element of the section and it takes you to a separate page. I've been producing versions of Collapsed Topics since Moodle 1.8 and publishing in the plugin's database so I don't understand what the major barriers there are? Kind regards, Gareth

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: wish: Design custom sections more accessible with closed sections
ResponsesInList.Text: Dear Gareth, we generally want to use the standard course format. I have deliberately suggested something that I know would be a quick win as the code for it already exists. If it were optionally possible to select that the themes are collapsed when opened, that would be great for accesibility in the standard courseformat. The operation of the collapsed theme is flawless. But using it is not easy for teachers with the setting options. Kind regards,

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: wish: Design custom sections more accessible with closed sections
ResponsesInList.Text: Dear Julia, Thank you for your reply. I'm intrigued by your comment of "But using it is not easy for teachers with the setting options" as I do want Collapsed Topics to be as intuitive and easy to use as possible with minimal amounts of supporting documentation. Thus any feedback I get, positive or negative is a good thing. I only tend to judge it by how I'd use and employ it in the classroom, which is where the spark for its development started. Kind regards, Gareth

ResponsesInList.Title: wish: Design custom sections more accessible with closed sections
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Julia, At the moment, the closest you can get to this is by updating the Course layout setting from "All Section one one page" to "Show one section per page" -- then the course begins with all sections essentially "closed" (but there is not toggle to open the sections, you have to view them on a separate page after clicking that section)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: wish: Design custom sections more accessible with closed sections
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello John, thanks for the tip. I also think that this is the only option so far. That's a good hint for many who are looking for a similar solution. However, we would like to use the default setting if possible for the following reasons: - Students want courses that are easy to navigate. The courses should be structured as similarly as possible in the navigation. - I really like the further development of the standard theme with the accordions. It offers consistency in operation. The accordions also make it possible to get a quick overview of individual sections. At the same time, the accordions are very clear when collapsed and can be accessed in just a few steps using the keyboard. However, “Show one section per page” has its own challenges: - Because the view is not fixed, it always looks different depending on whether images or more text are added. Although I know the course format well, I sometimes don't recognize it myself. As a result, I have sometimes not realized that I need to click on it because there is more content behind it. However, this will improve with 4.5 because there is now an arrow on the right. Also the behavior that you get to a sublevel when you click on a section title is now consistent as behavior in the Show all and Show one page variants. - In the past, we have created our own menus for the "Show one section per page" function. However, since I have been working on accessibility, I have come to the conclusion that a purely visual solution is not effective like this one from us: https://fhpcloud.fh-potsdam.de/s/H3kM4a9BoSpMbXM Kind regards, Julia

Note: Always install on a test server to confirm that the format does what you want it to do before updating or installing on a production server!  And as this release could contain bugs and so I strongly recommend that you check on a test server first!  Not sure how to set one up?  Then look at the 'Installer packages' on https://download.moodle.org/releases/latest/ . Ensure that you have multiple backups of all data before using.  Please report any issues. i.e. 'bugs' with this release ONLY here.  Before doing so please read 'Reporting issues' on the 'Information' tab on the course format 'Settings' under 'Site administration' -> 'Plugins' -> 'Course formats' -> 'Collapsed Topics'. ResponsesInList.Title: Are subsections really sections?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello, I've been looking at trying to make both Collapsed Topics and Grid formats work with subsections in Moodle 4.5 ( https://docs.moodle.org/405/en/Course_homepage#Add_a_subsection ).  As both formats retain the ability to alter the number of sections via a setting after the course has been created is problematic.  This has lead me to look at how things work, which has lead me to raise MDL-84038 (related to core functionality) which I then discovered links to MDL-83056 , were subsections are considered 'real sections' and should respect the 'maxsections' core setting. But... are subsections really 'sections' in a course but are actually a means of breaking apart a parent section?  On MDL-83056 in relation to subsections obeying 'maxsections', I've commented: I've been thinking about this and now it seems to me to be a bad idea. Take the situation where a user creates a course. They select the number of sections they want in the first instance. These 'sections' are full ones. Now if they have the maximum number of sections then go and discover that they can't add sub sections such that they can break apart the content in a section then they're going to get frustrated. They'll then have to deleted some sections (not what they want to do for the course design they have in mind) in order to add sub sections. Now the course is not structured in the way that they wanted in the first place. Therefore sub sections should not obey 'maxsections' but possibly have a new 'maxsubsections'. As when creating a course you can't say that I want ten sections with the third and fifth having two sub sections each. To me sections and subsections are two different things and shouldn't be restricted by the same thing.  Just like mixing up different units and thinking that the measurement represents the same thing. What do you think please?  Also comment on the respective tracker issues if desired. Gareth

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Are subsections really sections?
ResponsesInList.Text: I've been asking myself similar (ish) things recently. We're running into issues where a section exists and it might be nice to switch it into being a sub-section but to do this as far as I can tell you have to create a sub-section and then move the content into it and the same with going in the opposite direction. If a sub-section is indeed the same as a section then it would be good to share some expected functionality. Early days yet so I'm just off to find out where such comments may already have been made

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Are subsections really sections?
ResponsesInList.Text: Dear Kimberley, I've done a quick test and investigation and sub-sections are sections from a code point of view. Just that there is added data that allows them to be recognised as 'mod_subsection's too. That it is possible via database manipulation to convert a sub-section into a section. And perhaps, though I've not tried, to go the other way around. The complexity would be implementing this in the UI and specifying the exact place the section should be. Gareth

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Are subsections really sections?
ResponsesInList.Text: I suspect the only way in this instance is to backup in code the section you want to move, delete that section, then restore that section into the new subsection or otherwise. We've been using a course format that manages its own subsections, so we've decided not to use Moodle's subsection until we can get our heads around what changes we need to migrate. Obviously a better sidebar navigation experience is a motivator to switch to subsections.

It's a maelstrom of need to support both a page with all of the sections on and also having pages with a single section. The previous incarnation not only in CT was to have a 'Course layout' setting, but this confused users. I then implemented both with links to the single section page. However, there has been advancements with the Topics, now Custom format that allow it to solve this by having links to the single section page both in the Course Index and the actual course. When you return back from an activity in your scenario, you end up on the course page, when viewing, both the breadcrumb and course index are sectional bar one link in the breadcrumb that takes you back to the course page. With CT, it was always designed to solve the 'Scroll of death' by using 'toggles' long before the Topics, now Custom, format introduced them. To have a means by which it was possible to visualise all of the sections. Thus, I decided that it would be better to have the Course Index have 'Anchors' instead, a means of jumping to the section on the course page itself. The snag with this is that the links are 'cached' so the course format cannot be 'dynamic' and alter them depending on if you're on a single section page or not - a catch 22. Logically if you access a module from a single section page then you expect to be able to return to that page, when you access from a multiple section page then again you expect to be able to return to that page. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Anyone with hidden course sections shown as not available?
ResponsesInList.Text: Given that Visvanath, then perhaps there needs to be clarity upon which view should be the driving force? I see things as: The educators and educated drive the functional requirements of the tool they employ to facilitate learning. The administrators drive the functional requirements of the tool that empowers them to manage it for the educators and educated. The UX designers understand those requirements and come up with a design that matches, taking into account other requirements like accessibility . The developers implement the functional requirements taking into account the UX design within the limitations of the technology and available budget, be financial, time, or both. The managers manage an orchestrate the communication processes between all involved, thus bringing order to the potential chaos. There's an additional element here of 'change', or rather 'fear of change' and thus 'change management'.  Fear of change stifles creativity and progress.  We should always be thinking with a clear mind on what is the best solution for now, taking into account the lessons learnt from the past.  Just because we're used to what has been doesn't make it correct for the future. Thus in this case if the educators and educated consider that what already is, then this is the correct solution for the now and leave it alone.  Otherwise get the consensus from them of what it should be and implement it. Gareth

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Anyone using Social course format?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Helen, My thoughts -- I think it's a great idea to simply things and stick with one format versus having both since they are essentially the same. But,  but there are 2 great behaviors that are unique to Social Format that we'd lose if it were to be deprecated, so if both formats cold be 'combined' then I'd think that'd be the win-win 1. Social Format does not automatically Hide all other course activities when changing to this course format; whereas, Single Activity Format does automatically Hide all other activities in the course. Which behavior would be preferred? I dislike the the automatic Hiding because it ignores all the current visibility state set by the teacher for  the other course activities (and you can't plan ahead and set some things as Visible and some things in Stealth before changing formats). A teacher already has the option manually Hide or delete unneeded activities before changing the course to Single Activity Format, and attempting to change back these automatically Hidden activities back to Visible or Stealth after the fact is not straightforward and requires adding the Activities block or toggling between course formats a few more times. 2. The "Social Activities Block" can only be added to Social Format courses -- it would be extremely useful to also be able to add this into Single Activity Format courses (which would also help with issue 1 above so a teacher could just add new activities instead of figuring out how to get those automatically Hidden activities to be accessible). I see the "Social Activities Block" as essentially the same as the Front Page 's "Main Menu Block", just at the course-level. Example Use Case: a Scorm activity set to Single Activity Format could have a Feedback activity added into the "Social Activities Block" without the needing to manually paste a link into the Scorm Description area to directing users to a Stealth-ed Feedback activity in the course. So I almost feel Social Activities format (if it could be revised to allow it to be "any" activity, not just a forum) behaves better than Single Activity format...

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Anyone using Social course format?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, so sorry it took so long to reply to this! Here are some improvements we’d like to see with Social Format: 1.) A student can currently create a post from the main course page, somewhat like a social feed. However, once they click on “Post to Forum” the page navigates to the forum page. To make this more modern and in-line with expected user experience for students familiar with social sites, the student should stay on the main course page after posting and not be directed to a page with all of the forum topics. 2.) We should be able to add reactions to posts on the social format course page— for example thumbs up, smile, sad, etc. Most social platforms allow reactions currently and even Zoom has them. I think this is a feature that could be enabled or disabled within a particular course in case there are course settings where reactions are not appropriate. 3.) Currently, choosing “Discuss this topic” takes the student to a new page to post a reply. Instead, we would like the behavior to be more like modern platforms— when you click on ‘Discuss this topic’ a comment box should appear on the same page, without redirecting to another page. 4.) Ideally, the social format could integrate with giphy and have a button to add a gif to the reply. 5.) When students are replying to a topic, there should be buttons for recording audio or video as a response (without having to click, ‘Advanced’. All of these suggestions are to both bring the format up-to-par with modern social platform/ discussion / community expectations that students are already familiar with and to increase engagement for better social learning.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: audience based visibility
ResponsesInList.Text: @Anne, We've not found a way to hide courses from specific users, so we achieve this in two ways (depending on the course) The first way: Set up a course that will serve as an 'index' of the internal courses. Set up a custom menu (Site Admin > Appearance > Themes > Theme Settings) to point to this 'index' course. On this 'index' course, we add a Topic for each series of courses. Within each topic, we have a label (you could use URL activity as well) for each course. In the Restriction rules for each Topic, we set it to be hidden if the custom profile field is set to 0. That way the topic is hidden. In the "Overview" section of the course, we also add a label with some text stating that "These courses are restricted to employees of [Company Name]." with the Restriction set to hide the label if the custom profile field is set to 1. The second way we do this is using the AutoEnrol plugin. When setting up the AutoEnrol enrolment option for the course, we set the User Filtering to restrict it to the custom profile field set to 1. In the screenshot below, we do something similar, but with a different custom profile field. Make sure you disable any Self Enrolment options so the AutoEnrol option is the only option available. In the course description, we then have the text about the course being restricted. If a user that's not an internal user tries to enrol, they will see the normal enrolment screen, but no option to enrol and the text about it being restricted. If an internal user tries to enrol, they will be enrolled automatically via the AutoEnrol option.

ResponsesInList.Title: Add more activities to one Page
ResponsesInList.Text: Greetings, I am interested in developing courses that are presented in a single cohesive format, without the traditional separation into individual lessons. Instead, I envision a streamlined approach where users can access all course content on a single page. However, I also wish to include interactive elements such as quizzes and discussions at the end of the page, which may not be feasible within a single activity format. Is it possible to eliminate the need for lesson dividers and instead utilize a single-page format with multiple activities ? Thank you for your assistance!

ResponsesInList.Title: Add more activities to one Page
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Lucie, Just some thoughts depending how if you do not have too much content (a single page with a lot of content can get overwhelming). If you elect to use Single Activity Format, consider "Page" or "Book" format. Page is obviously one long page, where as Book would give you the option to add an additional "Page" if necessary (if a single Page activity is getting too long or too filled with content and scrolling) without the need to revision your entire course structure. Within the Page or Book, utilize Moodle's H5P plugin to embed interactive elements throughout your single activity (and these can link to the grade book). There's also the Embed Questions plugin where you can embed existing Quiz Questions from your course Question Bank throughout the activity as well (but I believe these would just be for practice without a gradebook assessment option). Whether you do a single activity course format or not, Stealth Mode is a great clutter reducing tool - it allows you add activities to your course page that are not visible upon an initial visit, but with Moodle Auto-Link Activity Names filter, these activities can appear as links in your single Page activity so users can access additional content without initially seeing it directly on the course page. To incorporate "Discussion", you could consider adding Moodle's Comments block add the Deft Response block plugin -- it sits in the Block panel (or if you're theme allows it, you can have it at the bottom of your Page activity, above the footer -- it allows a spot for users to leave comments with an optional prompt and optional poll capability too.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Add more activities to one Page
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi John, thank you for your response! To clarify my idea further: we aim to create microlearning lessons without nesting. When a user clicks on the course, there's no need for enrollment (we're using the autoenroll plugin), and they should immediately see the content. Each lesson will be presented on a single page, containing activities like quizzes or feedback sections , along with theme blocks and comment sections at the end. The goal is to keep everything on one page, eliminating the need for additional clicks or navigation. This project is designed for individuals who may not be proficient with digital technologies, so simplicity is paramount. To address content concerns, we'll ensure that no page contains an overwhelming amount of text. Instead, each page will consist of concise elements such as a title with a picture, one or two paragraphs of text, followed by an interactive activity, and additional text blocks. If I understand correctly, using the Book module would introduce additional pages, potentially leading to confusion for users due to nesting. Similarly, H5P activities would need to be presented as links, which might disrupt the seamless user experience. Regarding Stealth Mode, it operates similarly to the topic format, potentially complicating navigation and delaying access to quizzes. Please correct me if I am wrong. I am curious if there is another way to do this than single activity course + theme blocks.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Add more activities to one Page
ResponsesInList.Text: H5P (both the Blue core version and the black 3rd party plugin) can be embedded into the Page activity - there is an Insert H5P button in the atto text editor for the Core version and a Filter for the black 3rd party version, allowing you to insert H5P activities anywhere (not as a separate activity. Both will give you the interactivity you seek (but I'm not sure if the gradebook connects when its embedded, you'd have to try that out and see)

ResponsesInList.Text: That's a good workaround. But there are two problems in my case: 1. What to do if there are a lot of students? Manual activity completion will be a tedious process. 2. All five activities are quizzes and the completion condition is to get a passing grade so I can not override them.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Overriding course completion condition not changing completion status for existing students
ResponsesInList.Text: What i did in the past that worked for me in your situation provided you used "requires grade" or "requires submission" conditions. I edited the 5 activities' settings and for the Completion Conditions, I clicked the "Unlock Completion settings" button in each activity's settings. This essentially "reset" everything and then cron re-marks these activities as "done" with 2 exceptions -- (1) it will not automatically mark the "view the activity" condition as done after the reset (so students will have to view those activities again), and (2) it will not automatically mark the "students must manually mark the activity as done" (so students will have to mark those activities as done again).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Overriding course completion condition not changing completion status for existing students
ResponsesInList.Text: For the "Must View" or "Students Manually mark" issue: As Shirley said, use the Activity completion report here. Before you reset any activity, either open the Activity Completion report in two different browser tabs so you can do a before/after comparison, or download the Activity Completion report data. Then, do the reset in the settings of each of the activities and wait a few minutes for Cron to run. Finally, refresh one of the tabs that contained the Activity Completion report to see if there are boxes that did not get re-checked (such as ones that had "...must View..." or "...must Manually Mark..." conditions). Then you can toggle back and forth between the two browser tabs to manually mark those as done so the students don't have to go back and do it. Yup, it's a pain, but it works : )

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Overriding course completion condition not changing completion status for existing students
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Ashish, The completion status for the existing students should be recalculated when the scheduled task 'Calculate regular completion data' next runs. You can check that the task is running in Site administration > Server > Scheduled tasks. It is recommended to have it running every minute.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Grid format images blurry

ResponsesInList.Text: Adjust image resolution and check proper sizing for grid format to prevent noticeable blurriness, particularly in icons and graphical images. use optimal image quality settings and compress images through the moodle without losing their original quality or other online applications such as jpeg compressor .

ResponsesInList.Title: same course with two different names
ResponsesInList.Text: I want to add a course with two different names. Is there any way I can achieve this by adding single course content and linking it to two different names.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: same course with two different names
ResponsesInList.Text: No, not directly, and not with a straight out of the box Moodle. You could have 1 "content" course, and 2 "access" courses, and use something like Sub-course to turn the content course into an activity in the "access" courses. Otherwise you're looking at something closer to a repository model, where all your "course content" is held in a repository system, and then linked to 2 different Moodle courses. This however potentially changes in the future as more "content" can be stored in the Moodle Content Bank, but (I think) at the moment that is mostly just H5P content.

ResponsesInList.Title: COurse Start date and End date
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, can somebody help me ? I'm not sure if this is where should I ask this. I'm trying to check in the Database where exactly is the Start Date of Course and Course End date can be found? And I looked into mdl_course table and saw a column that says startdate and enddate, but the data doesn't make sense to me. can somebody help me with this?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: COurse Start date and End date
ResponsesInList.Text: Those are all Unix timestamps ( https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unix_time ) - the number of seconds since midnight on the 1st Jan 1970 UTC. These are used throughout the Moodle database. There are lots of ways to convert them into human-readable date / times, e.g. https://www.unixtimestamp.com/

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: COurse Start date and End date
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks for replying Davo!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: COurse Start date and End date
ResponsesInList.Text: If you're using mysql or mariadb you can use SELECT id, fullname, FROM_UNIXTIME(startdate) startdate, FROM_UNIXTIME(enddate) enddate FROM mdl_course;

We could get that information from the backup, and that problem was solved that same day. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Courses hidden when course format deleted
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Peter, I believe that sounds about right (to be an expected behavior). I believe disabling a plugin will essentially 'hide' it wherever it's used. But your warning is a good one -- best practice here might be to upload a CSV file through the Course Upload page to change the courses to a different format prior to uninstalling a plugin. You can also adjust visibility that way to if it's faster (and you already have all your course short names readily available)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Manage courses in different time periods.
ResponsesInList.Text: It is my understanding that Moodle does this for you. In that you set it up to be in your time zone, then when a user states their time zone in their profile, then this is used to make any adjustments.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Manage courses in different time periods.
ResponsesInList.Text: If you are talking about separate sections of the course, you have several options. You can copy the course for each section of students or you could create separate groups of students within the single course. If you are trying to create different due dates for each group of students you would either have to create separate courses or use the Relative Dates mode which allows you to set Assignment and Quiz due dates based on the enrollment date of the student.

ResponsesInList.Title: Activity information in course list not recognizing activity as complete but access restrictions does
ResponsesInList.Text: I have a course with activities that are scorm activities. Access to each activity is restricted based on the completion of the previous activity. Each activity (apart from the last one) has a small quiz at the end, but it doesn't matter if the student passes or fails, the activity returns "completed" after the quiz is taken so the student can continue on. Only the last activity is there a test that must be "passed" to be complete. After upgrading from moodle 3.9 to 4.1 I am having to contend with the new activity completion labels in the course activities list. (I would like the old tick boxes back but that is another discussion). The automatic-completion-conditions shows "To do: complete the activity", and yet the access restrictions consider the activity complete and so show the next activity as available to click on.  This is of course very confusing.  It seems that the new activity completion logic determines completion in a different way to access restrictions. I have found that the masteryoverride setting in scorm is on, and therefore the cmi.core.lesson_status is updated to passed or failed rather than completed, but it seems that regardless the course_modules_completion table contains an entry for the user with completionstate = 1. The activity completion settings on each activity is set to "require view" and "require status" = completed I have not be able to figure out yet how the new activity completion logic determines when an activity is complete. The screenshot illustrates the issue. The first activity is complete, hence the student is able to start the second one, but the activity information says it is not complete

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Activity information in course list not recognizing activity as complete but access restrictions does
ResponsesInList.Text: The activity completion settings on each activity is set to "require view" and "require status" = completed What happens when you remove the "require view" from the completion settings for an activity?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Activity information in course list not recognizing activity as complete but access restrictions does
ResponsesInList.Text: Removing "require view"  again results in the "to do: complete the activity" (but the access restriction succeeds and the course completion succeeds as well). An experiment was to change the completion criteria from "completed" to "passed". In this case the activity information shows it as "done". I also tried the experiment to have the completion criteria as "completed" but turn off the masteryoverride setting. In this case the activity information also shows it as "done". It seems, unlike the completion logic, the activity info is sensitive to whether cmi.core.lesson_status is set to "completed" or "passed"/"failed".

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Activity information in course list not recognizing activity as complete but access restrictions does
ResponsesInList.Text: SCORM activities are very picky that way. How the SCORM content is created in the publishing software determines which values can be used in the LMS. Kind Regards

ResponsesInList.Text: The SCORM publishing software is returning cmi.core.lesson_status "completed" (as I specified). It is moodle that is changing that to "passed" or "failed" based on the SCORM activity also returning a score and masteryoverride being set on. Nevertheless, this is handled by the completion logic that puts a record into the course_modules_completion table indicating the activity is complete. The activity info mechanism is however not in sync. It is obviously looking at other tables to calculate status, but I've not been able to figure out where it does this.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Activity information in course list not recognizing activity as complete but access restrictions does
ResponsesInList.Text: Is your scorm giving a grade - what if you just set the restriction to a specific grade?

This will work for students starting the course now, but for those part way through or who have completed it and going back to review they will see these confusing activity infos. It would be better if I could identify where it determines the activity status and bring it into line with the completion logic.

ResponsesInList.Title: Support more enrol methods in csv course upload
ResponsesInList.Text: Currently we support these enrolment plugins in course upload (Moodle 4.2): self guest manual We are extending course upload to support cohort and meta enrolments. Since a given course can can multiple enrolment instances of cohort and meta type we need to somehow uniquely identify the instance we would like to update by our csv. We can not use enroment instance name since those are not unique For cohort enrolment we can use cohort idnumber together with role. Cohort idnumber are unique, but we can use same cohort with different role to have another cohort enrol instance. But using them together does the trick. There is a drawback that cohort idnumber is not compulsory. So we need a proper documentation for user to be clear idnumber must be set for cohort to use it in csv course upload For meta enroment we can just use meta course shortname to uniquely identify enrol instance that we want to update in course since shortname is unique Relevant issues are MDL-73852 and MDL-73839 Now to the question. There are other enrol plugins that people might want to use in csv course upload - like fee plugin or lti plugin. Problem with those is that there is currently no way to uniquely identify which enrolment instance of given type you want to update in course. And course can have multiple enrol instances of lti or fee. If people need that to be supported in csv course upload we will need to refactor fee and lti enrol plugin to be able to distinguish between enrol instances. But first it would be good to know whether anyone will use it.

ResponsesInList.Title: How to override course/modeedit.php file in custom theme
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi , Would you please tell us that how to override course/modedit.php file in custom theme. I want to change somthing. Thanks.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to override course/modeedit.php file in custom theme
ResponsesInList.Text: If you're looking to change the styling of the page, then you can target it using the id tag of the 'body' element of the page (that will allow you to make styling changes to only that page). If the "something" you want to change is not related to the CSS of the page, then you probably can't change it using a theme (and depending on what that "something" is, there's a good chance you cannot change it without making changes directly to the core code).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to override course/modeedit.php file in custom theme
ResponsesInList.Text: If you're looking to add some new settings to the activity settings, you can add some functions in your theme's (or any plugin's) lib.php file to handle that, without changing core code (theme_yourtheme_coursemodule_standard_elements, theme_yourtheme_coursemodule_definition_after_data, theme_yourtheme_coursemodule_edit_post_actions). These functions handle how your data is displayed as a form, and how to handle the data if it is updated. I use it just to display some extra external data about assignments. You can see my use of it here: https://github.com/ltu-solent/moodle-local_solsits/blob/ca897be9687cd05ea72ada28bc64b38cee072fe5/lib.php#L36

MBA Students >> First Year >> Marketing Management >> Forecasting Economics students >> Second year>> Economics Planning >> Forecasting. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to use same course in Multiple categories (not duplicate or reuse)
ResponsesInList.Text: We have a similar situation and we had to go down the route of duplicates. In our case the course category is subject to where the student is based (AU or NZ). We ended up versioning our courses. The only downside is that when we create a new version of a course, students have to enrol in the new course and complete what they're already completed in the (now outdated) previous version of the course again. Each course in Moodle is treated independently and have no relation to any other course on Moodle in terms of content. There is no concept of a 'Template' course, which can be updated and any course 'based off' this template course is updated as well. If someone in the community has a solution for this, we'd be interested to know as well.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to use same course in Multiple categories (not duplicate or reuse)
ResponsesInList.Text: Yes, I agree. I had a word with some of you. There is no way this can be achieved. We have to duplicate each time.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to use same course in Multiple categories (not duplicate or reuse)
ResponsesInList.Text: In theory, it could be achieved with some custom code. If there is a file 'externservercourse.php' in the 'course' directory on the Moodle server , which contains the function 'extern_server_course', then that can be used to redirect the user to a different URL . The way it would be set up is the 'real' course is placed in one category, then empty courses are placed in the other categories. When a user visits one of the empty courses, then they are immediately redirected to the 'real' course. Unfortunately, when arriving at the 'real' course, it is listed in its actual category (not the category where you started), but it is a way of providing a sort of shortcut from a course in one place in the category tree, to another. It also requires a bit of coding, if you want a proper interface for setting up the links (rather than just hard-coding a bunch of course ids into the 'externservercourse.php' script).

ResponsesInList.Title: Course category only visible for selected users

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Course category only visible for selected users
ResponsesInList.Text: On the special category revoke (i.e. prevent) the view capability for the authenticated user role (which *everyone* normally holds) You'll then need to have a role defined that you can assign to the specific users that gives them back the view capability. Students aren't typically in the student role outside of a course context (where they are *enrolled*) so most of the general capabilities are set via the Authenticated User role.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Course category only visible for selected users
ResponsesInList.Text: So you need to go to /course/management.php and into the relevant category and assign the role there. However you need to make sure on your Role definition you have set it so that it can be assigned to category contexts.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Collapsed Topics is 14!
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Rick, Really interesting .  A few thoughts: Thank you for the compliments . CT (now) doesn't alter the database , but rather uses the core API to write data to and from existing tables.  Essentially to store the value of the settings and the current toggle state on a per user basis (the user preference functionality).  Although I always stress to test on a test server first. At some point (I think in MDL-35770 of 14th November 2012) core introduced the 'coursedisplay' setting where by you could either have all topics on one page or one topic per page.  This is what CT had until in version 3.3.0.3 for Moodle 3.3 I dropped this in favour of the 'one section' icon (dot within a circle) that takes you to the single section page.  However, I believe you state this was in CT back in the M2.x versions? Possibly have sub-titles for accessibility ? I really like the comparisons and understanding of how you use the format, and how it matches your style.  It strikes me, in a positive way, that the course with the topics collapsed is like a table of contents in a technical reference book.  Thus as such, you only tend to look up what you want and read about specific bits rather than having to digest everything in one go or when you're looking something up again, you can go straight there. Good point with section 0, in fact it has always been that way.  But I'm now thinking that having seen what you've shown that perhaps on the single section page it should not be shown and yet still remain on the main course page.  A setting perhaps to state 'show on single section page' on / off.  Thus it remains on the main course page because of its importance but is actually clutter on the single section page because the student needs to concentrate on that specific material and knows they can always navigate back to the main course page to find it. Kind regards, Gareth

ResponsesInList.Title: Course Restore with existing users enrolled
ResponsesInList.Text: We are in the process of merging two Moodle sites into a single site, including courses and enrolments. Both sites are on Moodle v3.11. Site A contains the courses and users that will be moved to Site B. The courses and users don't exist in Site B. When we backup the first course (including enrolments)  from Site A and restore it on Site B, the users are created and enrolled, as expected. When we repeat this processes for the next course, we get a "Trying to restore user 'REDACTED' from backup file will cause conflict" for every user enrolled in the course. We assume this is because the user now already exists and can't be created again. However, we still need said user to be enrolled in the restored course. What is the best way to restore the courses, including enrolments?

ResponsesInList.Title: Permalinks to course sections
ResponsesInList.Text:
Dear All, I believe there is a strong need to finally add the option to link permanently to course sections . Each course section has its own unique ID, clearly visible in the URL when editing it (cf. e.g:  Edit > <you_site_URL>/course/editsection.php? id=18724 &sr ). I have just added a comment to this tracker item: https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-62323 "Preserve links to sections" , after earlier reading this 2018 discussion . I'm reproducing that comment below. Perhaps some Moodlers will want to comment and/or upvote that tracker issue. * * * It is possible to use permalinks to sections but ONLY when in the editing mode: I tested using the "Show all sections on one page" layout of the Topics format A link such as /course/view.php?id=292#sectionid-18724-title can lead me to the right heading and part of the page: <h3 id="sectionid-18724-title" class="sectionname"> Here's a screenshot: UNFORTUNATELY, when Editing is turned off , that unique ID identifier for the section disappears , and the H3 element becomes: <h3 class="section-title"> only. If the section ID was retained , we would gain the possibility of linking to the
section regardless of its placement in the course's numbered section
list - at least for "All sections on one page" scenarios. There is a more global need to add something like
"permalinks" to course sections that would work with any (core) course
format.

ResponsesInList.Text: Moodle 4.2 will feature permanent links to course sections: https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-76418 "Have a way to get the permalink to a course section (and probably also to a section number)" The method described in the tracker works manually also with lower Moodle versions (3.11.*, 4.0.*) (though links might not work with all course formats).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Permalinks to course sections
ResponsesInList.Text: BTW , links like /course/view.php?id=16&section=3 are NOT permalinks, of course. If you move the section, its number in the course structure changes. That's why for permalinks the option with the unique ID attribute like "sectionid-###-title" was utilised. However, it appears not to be robust enough in comparison to the existing "section"-based addresses - in Collapsed Topics at least - from what I have seen. In the core Topics, Moodle 4.0.7, with one-section-per-page setting, the permalink will default to the main course page without opening the one targeted section (and sometimes - I think - not scrolling down at once to the target right section title). But then, probably best implementation of the permalinks will be from Moodle 4.2 up.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Permalinks to course sections
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, not 100% sure if it's related to this discussion, but I feel it somehow is: You maybe also want to have a look at MDL-75542 . There, I added a new parameter "expandsection" (for example "/course/view.php?id=12345&expandsection=3") to the course view page to forcibly expand a section so you can use an anchor to an activity to jump right where you want you be. The patch also contains an API extension to the course formats, so course formats from now on have the opportunity to use this parameter and implement what should happen in their format if this is being specified, for example expand the section. For topics and weeks this already is being implemented in MDL-75542 , all other course formats just need to use it. Feel free to raise issues in their trackers, if they do not support this yet Also be aware that this feature will only be available from Moodle 4.2 onwards.

ResponsesInList.Title: Random Course Completions error - invalid course dependency
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi We're using Moodle 3.9 and a theme called Epsilon (based on Boost) and are experiencing a recurring error with Course Completion settings: existing courses suddenly (apparently random, and with no discernable cause) have a new Course Completion setting set - a completion dependency on another course, but there is no "other course" selected. This of course means that the Course Completion report can't be run. We are able to fix this issue when it occurs - we open the Course Completion settings and remove the dependency on the non-existent course. Of course that means that we lose all the existing activity completions for the course but those are usually automatically recovered by Moodle. So this isn't a showstopper problem, but it's still annoying. This seems to affect about one course per month - including courses that have not been touched by anyone - and we have no idea why. Is anyone else experiencing this issue? If so, do you have any idea what causes it? Have you identified the characteristics of courses that get affected in this way?  Have you found a fix for it? Stan

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Random Course Completions error - invalid course dependency
ResponsesInList.Text: Dear Stan, Have to looked in the logs to see if there is anything there that identifies how the dependency is added? G

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Random Course Completions error - invalid course dependency
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Gareth - thanks for your response. Yes, I've looked at the logs and no, there is nothing that suggests how that course-completion dependency is added. Of course these are real courses and there are pages (sometimes hundreds of pages) of logs for each, so I'm focusing on "Course Completion changed" events - if it got logged as something else I'd be unlikely to find it. All events logged in these courses are the expected events for a course - there are no "Unknown event" entries or similar oddities. A lot of our courses are created by restoring (via moosh) a backup of a "template" course, which also restores the course-completion criteria. So in most cases, the very first "Course Completion changed" logged event is the one where the problem was fixed. This error - a course-completion dependency, but without a course being selected - is impossible to create by a user, so I'm confident that it's not user-driven. I've tested this, and if a user tries to add a course-completion dependency but doesn't select a course the dependency is not added. Stan

ResponsesInList.Title: Hidden categories and hiding courses within them
ResponsesInList.Text: Kia ora forum contributors, long time reader, first time asker here Please help!  I need to be able to hide a specific category from teaching staff AND include hiding the courses in that category on the teachers dashboard .  While I can edit the category permissions so the teacher cannot see the category in category view, it does not prevent the courses within that category displaying on the teachers dash - that is because the teacher is enrolled in that course. Issues Teachers cannot be removed from the courses that are in the hidden category, as these courses are subsequently linked to courses which are not in hidden categories. Teachers must be able to see other hidden courses, as long as the Category they are in is visible. Backstory... Conduit creates courses with students / staff attached (we call these "feeder" courses), these have no content only Participants.  We then create a "manual course" (using copy course or backup/restore), which has content, then we meta-link anywhere from one to 50+ feeder courses to this "manual" course.  The "manual" course is hidden initially, but when ready the teachers can unhide. The feeder courses for years now have caused confusion, as they appear as empty shells on the teachers dashboard.  The feeder courses are not visible to students as they stay hidden. I've tried to explain this as simply as possible, my apologies if I have not been clear.  I'm relatively new to Moodle, and this was an issue 6+ years prior to my starting.  We would really appreciate some guidance please.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Hidden categories and hiding courses within them
ResponsesInList.Text: In core moodle, there is no way to hide just some hidden courses, unless you do something like this... Duplicate the teacher role and call it something like Conduit Teacher or whatever makes sense to you. For the permissions for that role, remove the ability to see hidden courses. Give the teachers the new role in the courses that you do not want them to have access it. It is possible that you could also do this at the category level with role that can be applied at the category level - again, removing the ability for them to see the courses in that category.

Therefore I've created https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gjb2048/moodle-format_grid/c058a98b067e012cbd39a121c8ea48951db6dc37/db/upgrade.php which is a direct replacement for the version in V4.0.1.0 to cope when there is an error the first time you perform the upgrade, and subsequently needing to update again. Because the format version has not changed, i.e. updated, then the update element will execute again, detect that you already have a 'format_grid_image' table, delete and recreate it, then cope with what might of happened. I've only tested this 'once' and only where I manipulated the data in the database to mimic what I was told. Therefore, as usual, I cannot stress enough that you need to test first on a test server that is a direct replicant of your production server to ensure that everything should be fine when you update on production and always have a backup or more!  Note: The 'format_grid_icon' must still be there for the second run to operate as it should.

ResponsesInList.Title: Beta Grid for Moodle 4.0
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello, I have updated the Grid format for Moodle 4.0 as follows: Version 4.0.0.1 for Moodle 4.0 version 2022041900.00 (Build: 20220419) and above within the MOODLE_400_STABLE branch until the next release: https://moodle.org/plugins/format_grid/4.0.0.1/27419 https://github.com/gjb2048/moodle-format_grid/releases/tag/V4.0.0.1 with: Start of complete re-build from scratch - functionality added as funded.  Decision made due to the changes in the core API. A little backstory The course format API in Moodle 4.0 has been almost completely changed the way that course formats operate.  The old methods have been deprecated leading to lots of warning messages on development systems and future removal of that functionality causing the format to no longer operate.  Through the work done on Collapsed Topics, I have been able to understand the true nature of what needs do be done to update a course format and came to the conclusion that it was too big a job for the Grid format in one go.  With change there is opportunity, with time there is feature creep, and so this first version of the format for Moodle 4.0 is the first step providing initial functionality of uploading an image, having it shown in a grid and having that link to a section on a single section page.  Gone is the old method of uploading an image with a custom form, being replaced with a section setting: The course settings: 'Set the image container width', 'Set the image container ratio relative to the width', 'Set the image resize method' and 'Show the grid image in the section summary' have been retained along with their global defaults.  The course setting 'Number of sections ' remains instead of increasing and decreasing sections. If you have existing courses or backups from a previous version, then the images should be retained upon upgrade / restore.  It is the intent to progressively add back functionality if it's actually wanted. I strongly suggest that this version is installed on a test server only!  It is a 'beta' release!  Ensure that you have backups, in at least two different places, of all data before using.  Even better, run on an install on a virtual machine. If you find this post useful, then please mark it so.  Please report any issues with this version ONLY here. Gareth

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Aaron, I think it would be enough to use separate group mode in your course. - in course administration, set group mode to separate - then add four course groups - add your students to the right course group - optionally add the faculty/teaching staff to the group as well - optionally use group overrides to define different start/due dates per group (not supported by all activities , but the big ones like assignments and quizzes do) Then you can use just one course for all your students and this the standard course completion report will be enough for your reporting needs.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Entering the course on highlighted topic
ResponsesInList.Text: Ivana, you have hit upon some interesting "how do you manage topics in a course" questions. I know of no way to automatically put students into a highlight topic. Sorry. I know of no automatic way to reorder topics so that the current topic is first. Sorry. As far as I know, none of the four major LMSs (B, C, D, or M) can do what you wish to do. In all four LMSs, you can manually reorder topics. I thought about reordering topics, as you suggest,  20 years ago when I began using Blackboard.  I recall doing it the first time that I used Blackboard, and it was a pain to do so. So I always keep my topics arranged from first to last, sequentially. Yes, drag-and-drop makes moving topics around easier, but it is still too time consuming and error prone. So even though it might make so sense to you, I would suggest that if you were to do this for a course that had, for example, 20 topics, you would eventually abort. On the positive side of things: Moodle is the only major LMS that allows you to highlight the current topic. This is an extremely valuable feature, one that even students love, so that everyone knows what the current topic is. However, it is still up to the instructor to remember to manually highlight the current topic, and many instructors find this to be too much work (yep, less than a minute) or do not know that Moodle supports this feature. (I and others in the Canvas Community have asked Canvas to add this feature, but Canvas doesn't understand why it is important to highlight the current topic. Oh well.) In my courses, I use the Collapsed Topics plugin, which allows students to compress topics that are finished. Collapsed topics will remember which topics they have closed. (Canvas has a similar feature, but when students enter a course, all topics are always open.) Moodle provides "activity completion" checkboxes that instructors can set up. This is an extremely valuable feature that allows students to know which activities they have completed. D2L had this feature. BB and Canvas do not. (I and others in the Canvas Community have asked Canvas to add this feature, but Canvas doesn't understand why it is important to highlight the current topic. Oh well.) So you might be left showing your instructors these valuable Moodle features, along with what features do not exist, and hope that you instructors will use them to their advantages. I give my students this video that explains how I structure my courses.  Take note of video chapter marker 5, Topics, chapter; and chapter marker 14, Checklist and Activity Completion.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Entering the course on highlighted topic
ResponsesInList.Text: Sidenote: Canvas does have activity completion checkmarks available in the Modules. Moodle's version can be made to more specific criteria, but for Canvas, you can apply these checkboxes to every single listing and is always found in a consistent spot, so it is easy for students to track when an item should be completed (open circle), completed (green checkmark), or past due (red)

Improve documentation for Toggle blocks location' functionality - https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=428924 and #100. Improve user enrolment event handling to be more efficient for activity information - #114. Separate out 'Activity information' as a separate reset, new capability 'changeactivitymeta' and fix the 'forum' module in the list of enabled plugins so that it can be enabled and the others disabled and 'showadditionalmoddata' still take effect. Added 'courseadditionalmoddatamaxstudents' setting to restrict, if desired, the display of the activity information on a a course of the number of students on that course exceeds it.  When 'showadditionalmoddata' is enabled on a course, then additional information about the status of this is shown underneath the setting on the course settings page.  This is so that large courses can be automatically prevented from showing the information as the calculations would take an unacceptable amount of time to compute.  It is up to the administrator to set the figure based upon benchmarking / testing of the performance characteristics of the server .  The default is '0', which means 'unlimited' number of students. Version 3.8.1.6 for Moodle 3.8 version 2019111800.00 (Build: 20191118) and above within the 3.8 branch until the next release: https://moodle.org/plugins/format_topcoll/3.8.1.6/25465 https://github.com/gjb2048/moodle-format_topcoll/releases/tag/V3.8.1.6 with: Add 'enableadditionalmoddata' setting to turn on / off additional information at a site level.  Default is 'off'! Separate out 'Activity information' as a separate reset, new capability 'changeactivitymeta' and fix the 'forum' module in the list of enabled plugins so that it can be enabled and the others disabled and 'showadditionalmoddata' still take effect. Added 'courseadditionalmoddatamaxstudents' setting to restrict, if desired, the display of the activity information on a a course of the number of students on that course exceeds it.  When 'showadditionalmoddata' is enabled on a course, then additional information about the status of this is shown underneath the setting on the course settings page.  This is so that large courses can be automatically prevented from showing the information as the calculations would take an unacceptable amount of time to compute.  It is up to the administrator to set the figure based upon benchmarking / testing of the performance characteristics of the server.  The default is '0', which means 'unlimited' number of students. I strongly suggest that you test on a test server first!  With the addition of the 'enableadditionalmoddata' setting, the default is 'No' so unless you explicitly set it to 'Yes' then you'll find that all of the activity information in your courses will NOT show regardless of the course settings.  This is because the primary objective of the format is to make the use of the course page easier, not harder by slowing down the page load.  I've also added the 'courseadditionalmoddatamaxstudents' setting to curtail the performance impact of large courses, this you need to test and decide for yourself what is a suitable value for your system. If you find this post useful, then please mark it so.  Please report any issues with these versions ONLY here. Gareth
