ResponsesInList.Title: Grid format updated for Moodle 3.9 and 3.10
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello, These releases supersede: moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=422149 . Version 3.10.1.2 for Moodle 3.10 version 2020110900.00 (Build: 20201109) and above within the 3.10 branch until the next release: github.com/gjb2048/moodle-format_grid/releases/tag/V3.10.1.2 moodle.org/plugins/format_grid/3.10.1.2/24232 Version 3.9.1.3 for Moodle 3.9 version 2020061500.00 (Build: 20200615) and above within the 3.9 branch until the next release: github.com/gjb2048/moodle-format_grid/releases/tag/V3.9.1.3 moodle.org/plugins/format_grid/3.9.1.3/24231 with: Fix grid image placement for RTL languages. Fix missing 'set' prefix on 'section0ownpagenogridonesection' causing offset error on course restore. Fix 'PNG files not transparent' - #142. Outstanding issue: github.com/gjb2048/moodle-format_grid/issues/143 - s o, I propose that instead of a fairly terminal error, that the following image be displayed in the grid with the 'error information' being in the alternative text: What do people think please?  The code area that generates these errors will fail because the underlying PHP image functions fail to operate correctly with the image uploaded / PHP image functions not available. Important note: The M3.10 version differs from the M3.9 version in that I've moved quite a few of the functions from lib.php to an autoloaded 'toolbox.php' file, this is something I've been meaning to do for years as, I believe, lib.php is always loaded but for a plugin 'locallib.php' is not, and so I've gone beyond that and used the next generation of that being 'Automatic class loading' ( docs.moodle.org/dev/Automatic_class_loading ).  The consequence of this is that the 'refactor' may contain errors, even though I've done my best and tested as much as possible.  Thus, please as with all plugin updates, install on a test server first and thoroughly check that everything is as expected! Please report any issues with these versions here ONLY.  If you find this post useful, then please mark it so. I am aware that M3.11 has been released and it is my intent to publish updates to 'Grid', 'Collapsed Topics' and 'Foundation', with updates to 'Theme Selector' and 'SynHi' if needed.  'Adaptable' is another subject and will likely follow the same pattern as M3.9 -> M3.10. Gareth

ResponsesInList.Title: Collapsed Topics updated for Moodle 3.10
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello, I've updated Collapsed Topics for Moodle 3.10 as follows: Make engagement information optional - #80 and #91 - thanks to Nina Herrmann ( https://github.com/NinaHerrmann ) for the enhancement. All course settings now have an option to track the value of the global default as set by the administrator.  Thus, when they change, then the course changes without any user interaction on the course.  The reset course functionality is still there and will set the value of the setting to the this 'new' default value.  The default colour value is '-' and the colour picker box will show the colour that has been set as the default.  All other settings will state what the default currently is. You can get it from: moodle.org/plugins/pluginversion.php?id=23213 .  All being well, I'll backport the new default functionality as I spotted a few bugs when implementing the code.  They are not worth fixing as the new functionality resolves them. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Sending message to all users that have not complete a course
ResponsesInList.Text: Hey Melanie, FWIW, we do use a partner to host the production Moodle instance (only our demo playground is self hosted). We did talk to them regarding Workplace as there were a number of major gaps in Moodle core that we see as beneficial in Workplace: Programmes and the ability to reuse courses within other areas Certifications: period based (relative) not date based and reoccurrence (i.e. need to sit the same course each year). Importing users and automatically assigning them to the correct course. Hierarchical structure Manager/Teams member etc However, we also discussed the maturity of the Workplace platform and the ability to "work around" issues in Moodle. Of the list above, we have "worked around" (or believe we could work around): 1) The lack of Programs are a severe limitation in current Moodle core, but with some clever use of Meta course linking, I think we can provide a workable solution. 2) Moodle v3.8 has experimental use of relative course dates (about bloody time). 3) (with a bit of faffing) as we have managed to get Azure AD synced with Moodle and users provisioned into specific courses (with a few additional plugins) That just leaves Hierarchical staff structures, which we can live without for the time being. In addition, we use Arlo as a platform for organising our OnPrem training, which integrates with Moodle. This is likely to become very  important this year as we start to push OnPrem and eLearning together.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Sending message to all users that have not complete a course
ResponsesInList.Text: Course completion will do this for you. Choose the individual activites you want completed. Course completion tracks those. Then Course completion report Course completion info can be viewed by managers, teachers and non-editing teachers (and any other users with the capability report/completion:view) in Administration> Course administration > Course completion or via a link in the Course completion status block. The report will send mass emails to students you select. Warning: you want to think carefully about which activities your want marked complete and what the criteria will be. I'm also not sure you can turn course completion on if you are already active in the course. If you can, then a quick and dirty would be to have one activity to mark complete (say, a quiz) and call it This is The Last Thing To Do To Complete Your Course. One question with a score of one will complete the activity and show up on the course complete report.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Course not complete but showing 100% on dashboard
ResponsesInList.Text: The dashboard is reporting completion of activities , not whether or not the course has been 'completed' according to course completion criteria. Not everyone uses course completion. I have courses which the dashboard will never show 100% on because the users have either/or criteria and if the don't do both, it says they are not 100% complete--but they get a certificate and are told they are done. And I have other courses that show 100% even though the student has not passed the class because they have completed (no pass judgement) all the activities and students complain that they didn't get credit--they completed the work but they didn't complete it with passing scores. Would it be nice if it actually ran on completion, yes. But since many users don't use course completion, it wouldn't help them. It is just supposed to be informational, not the final word. The dashboard doesn't say you have completed the courses, it says you have completed all activities. It doesn't tell you the status of your grade or if you failed the class completely but performed all required activities. If all the requirements have been done, you still get 100% on the dashboard. It is a bit irritating but that's what it does...And that's why my boss hates the dashboard. It is really only great at saying, Hey! You're enrolled in these courses and can do stuff in them! and Hey, you were enrolled in these courses but they're over now! or Hey, there's a course you need to take! But you can't go there yet!... On a positive note...at least the dashboard recognizes *all* activities (and resources, I think) now and not just two or three--in moodle 1.x, it only would reflect a couple of activities and then, not consistently. So this is an improvement!

It's entirely feasible that shortnames would be the same for similar courses in different categories: Form 1 -> English and Form 2 -> English : and since the shortname is a field that is visible in the interface, it makes more sense to the end user to use a friendly name rather repeating bits or adding numbers. E.g. Dashboard > Courses > Form 1 > English > Week 2 > Introduction makes more sense than either Dashboard > Courses > Form 1 > F1_English > Week 2 > Introduction Dashboard > Courses > Form 1 > English_3 > Week 2 > Introduction I've read discussions in the tracker and years-old forum posts relating to uniqueness and none have led me to solid documentation on whether the shortname field must be unique for any particular reason, or if the schema or interface is the correct way. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: [3.7] Are shortnames supposed to be unique or not?
ResponsesInList.Text: The course shortname must be unique. This is and has always been so. This is enforced in the code in /course/lib.php in the function create_course (lines 2392 et seq. in 3.7.) See screenshot. If you try to create a new course with a duplicate shortname or change the shortname of an existing course to one already in use, you will get the error "Short name is already used for another course." If you try to creat a new course in the Site admin > Courses > Course upload tool with a duplicate shortname, you will get the error: "The course exists and update is not allowed" because the shortname is already used. And if you set the Course upload mode to "Create new courses, or update existing ones", it will not make a new course but will update the already existing course that has that shortname. This is a constraint in the code, not in the table but you will notice that all the table indices for mdl_course are all either unique or refer to other items that are unique. Changing the code to allow duplicates would not be a trivial task. It would be far, far easier to change your theme so that the breadcrumb and or the NavDrawer would show what you prefer there. Randy

ResponsesInList.Title: Induction Course (complete first and then "unlock" more the rest courses)

Otherwise, if you use course self-enrolment, a workaround is to add a final activity at the end of course 1 - such as a quiz - inside which you give the enrolment key to the next course (in the quiz feedback for example, or in a label using access restrictions based on passing the quiz). ResponsesInList.Title: Best way to set up course
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi all I have experience working at 2 registered training organisations in Australia. One institute set up their courses with the individual units as individual courses metalinked to a course page. I was told this offers better tracking and flexibility. I didn't really think too much of it until one day the integration with Jobready broke down and I was tasked with doing student extensions. Thus, I had to go into each individual unit(course) and extend it manually which was a pain. Some diplomas had 16 units so going through each unit took time. My current RTO has the courses set up using tiles so all units are contained in the one course. I was just wondering what is the better setup, each unit as its own course or putting all the units into the one course? Are their any real advantages doing one way over another? I would like to hear from any other moodle admin people in the RTO sector or TAFE and what has been their experience. Thanks.

ResponsesInList.Text: Anyway, getting back on track to your original question... this is quite difficult to achieve in Moodle (which is possibly why you’re not getting many replies with suggestions). You could do a custom report using a plugin such as Configurable Reports or the Ad Hoc Reports plugin. Possibly even the Course Completion Overview plugin might tell you what you need to know, but it’s slightly out of date now. You could possibly use some of the plugins to help you manage enrolment ( https://moodle.org/plugins/enrol_attributes ) and/or membership of cohorts (eg. https://moodle.org/plugins/auth_mcae ) , but the effort of keeping the profile fields up to date defeats the object tbh. Another LMS has this type of workflow built in to their Programs feature but has a substantial subscription cost compared with a free licence for Moodle. Moodle for Workplace may have something similar when it’s released, but will also cost money. So unfortunately, I suspect you’re between a rock and hard place. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Grid format install removed number of sections drop down in course format

ResponsesInList.Title: Grid format beta pre-release with WebP support on M3.6
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello, I've added WebP ( developers.google.com/speed/webp ) support for the displayed images in the Grid format.  Moodle itself does not support this new image format (at the time of typing) as it is not a known mime type, so you won't be able to upload WebP images but the format will do the conversion for you.  The mime type 'image/webp' is served and you will need a supporting browser ( caniuse.com/#feat=webp ). WebP is a new image format for the web that reduces the size of images, therefore page load times should be faster. To use, change the 'defaultdisplayedimagefiletype' setting to 'WebP' as an administrator as per the screen shots attached. If things don't work out, then just change the 'defaultdisplayedimagefiletype' setting back to 'Original' and things 'should' be fine again. As this is a 'pre-release' you can initially get the code from github.com/gjb2048/moodle-format_grid/releases/tag/V3.6.0.3 .  I strongly suggest that you only use a test server in the first instance.  If all goes well, then I'll release formally in the plugins database . Gareth

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Trying to design courses

ResponsesInList.Text:
Hello, I'm not sure if this is the correct place to post this, but I'm
trying to create a course that requires 500 points to pass each section. Each
section has activities that are different point values (100, 50, 15...) and a
student gets that amount of points when they pass or complete an activity. The course is completed when all sections have 500 or more
points. I have been looking at points and scales, but neither seem
to be able to do this. It looks like a hack may be to assign a scale to each

points. But I don't know where to go from there. How do I do this? What documentation should I read? Thank you,

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Making a Point Based Course?
ResponsesInList.Text: You could consider is having a gradebook category for each section of content in the course. Then add a Page module (which could simply be text that congratulates the students for completing the section) to the end of each section of content and restrict the page module to be available only once students have earned a certain amount of points for that gradebook section. Then you can set the course completion to be dependent upon the students opening each of the "page modules" that are in the sections.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Making a Point Based Course?
ResponsesInList.Text: Agree with John, generally.  Keep in mind...if you have some activities that have a required score, setting a course grade to pass might undermine that--if there are 500 points and 5 activities where you want 80% or better to pass each activity.  With a required course grade of 400 (80%), a participant could score 50/90/100/100/70 and still 'pass' with 410 points--and that is with two failed activities.  You might want to add activity completion requirements as well that, using John's example, only allow the last thing to display when you reach each requirement. And be clear about the requirement--you must have 80% on each activity AND 80% overall.  Sometimes students try to game the system. Most activities have a grade by default (either one assigned on completion--quiz, scorm , lesson --or one you give manually--forums, glossary or assignments).  You can set restrictions to require specific scores/completion before the next one is done as well.

ResponsesInList.Text:
Thanks for this thread everybody, Just like Mary I never realised that one can actually link to orphaned sections. It looks like you were exploiting the bug in Moodle behavior as a feature. To summarise what was set above, here are the reproduction instructions (on Moodle 3.2 or earlier): Set up a course in "topics" format to display one section per page Add activities to every topic and then decrease the number of sections down to 0 Add nice buttons to "general section" with links to pages http://YOURSITE/course/view.php?id=12345&section=1 ; http://YOURSITE/course/view.php?id=12345&section=2 ; ... When student opens the course page they only see the buttons and do not see sections headings student will be able to follow the links and the sections will be displayed with all activities they contain (one per page) I must say, Moodle users are very creative! I would never think of doing that, I would just install a course format that does buttons for you. I'm pretty sure Grid format was designed exactly for this scenario. This is what I can recommend you in Moodle 3.3 to keep this behavior: After upgrade all orphaned sections will automatically become "hidden". You will need to unhide sections one by one. Now you need to hide the links to the sections from the course main page. You can do it by adding the CSS : 
```text
ul.topics li.section-summary { display:none}
```
 How can you add CSS? There are multiple options for it. If you are an admin on the site, you can add it to "Custom CSS" in your theme settings. In this case it will apply to ALL courses in topics format that have "display one section per page" setting. If you are an admin but want to apply to one course only you'll need to prefix it with course-specific identifier: " body.course-12345 ul.topics li.section..." (where 12345 is the course id) If you are not an admin you can add CSS style somewhere in your course, for example in general section summary or as a label. You need to disable Atto editor in your preferences to do it because Atto will remove <style> tag. See screenshot As I said, these are all just workarounds and hacks to make the "Topics" format look like some other course format. The best solution will be to use the proper course format.

ResponsesInList.Title: Activate past courses for a user when he's enrolled in a new one
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello everyone! Please help with some ideas how to best organize this. We add users to courses for a period of time. After this period their access to course ends. But when this user takes another course, we'd love to make past courses visible for them automatically. Is there a way to do it? Is there a way to add users via file and set the expiration date for their whole profile, for example? So when we again add them from a file to a new course, the whole profile is activated and they can access all past courses. This option would be great but I can't find if it's possible. Thank you for your thoughts!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Activate past courses for a user when he's enrolled in a new one
ResponsesInList.Text: I do not believe this can be done in any practical manner. A number of people have tried it, but I have never heard of anyone being successful. Having said that there is a possibility, but it will require some creative course structuring and I am not sure it is workable. These are just thoughts and are convoluted. I am sure someone else may have a better suggestion, but you never know until some discussion gets going. 1. Categories are set up on a single division, say by year-semester, e.g. 2018-19S1 and 2018-19S2 or any practicable division you can make. 2. Each Category contains the sub-Categories, e.g Math, Science, Humanities, Social Science, or whatever subdivision makes sense in your setting, and each sub-Category contains the courses or more sub-sub-Categories as required. 3. Students are enrolled in the courses in the appropriate, main, single division, e.g. A User is enrolled in both Underwater Basket Weaving, short name of UBW89S1, and Blowing Glass, short name of BG89S1, in the 2018-19S1 Category. Those courses are completed, but the User remains enrolled in those courses. The User then enrolls in the 2018-19S2 course of Glass Weaving 1, short name of GW189S2. In the meantime, the Underwater Basket Weaving, short name of UBS89S2, course is running in 2018-19S2 as well and has been cloned to the appropriate Category, 2018-19S2. As long as Categories are separate and short names are different, this should work. There are, however, a number of problems that will, inevitably, arise.  The first is the size of your Moodle. Duplicating courses like this is always taxing on space, sooner or later. Another is the database . The database gets larger and larger, in a relatively short space of time so will need more and more space. Can you afford that kind of space? You have backups that get larger and larger, restores get more and more tricky, and the whole thing is likely to collapse under its own weight. Updates become more complex and upgrades can be seriously fraught. Adding new courses, dropping off old ones, and so on, these things can become increasingly difficult to maintain. This demands a high level of commitment from support staff as well, which is not always appropriate or welcome on their part. Obviously, anything can be done with hugely infinite disk space and memory and server speed, but that costs, and a lot of cost I would think. It is also why I suspect it is impractical to consider. Having said that, if the average enrollment in your Moodle is three or four years, you can have two Moodles. One that keeps materials in it for the length of enrollment, the other as an archive that retains materials for another three or four years. Each year is meticulously backed up and carefully stored as it falls off the end of the second Moodle. If a User returns outside that period then a year level could be restored so that Users can review the courses they have completed. Again, this requires a level of commitment from support staff to maintain, lower than the previous section, but still higher than would probably be liked. Good luck.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Activate past courses for a user when he's enrolled in a new one
ResponsesInList.Text: This is a much simpler idea, and considerably more workable. I don't know your exact circumstances, but if you are an education institute then as long as the User is enrolled in your institute, they will continue to be enrolled in your Moodle. If a business, as long as they are employed by your business, then they remain in the Moodle. Simple, Moodle is responsive to the greater requirement of your operation. The issue here will be the number of enrollments in your course. How many Users do you have in your most popular course this year? How many Users will be in that course next year. I suspect this is why you will need to archive your courses, but the courses can be cloned without past Users to allow a new set of Users without affecting past enrollments of Users. I also suspect this is the problem that everyone who has tried to resolve this runs into and can't find an adequate, workable solution.

The requirement here is that badges that have already been taken can't be retaken again on later courses by that student. I've looked at course settings and it seems that there are only two options for course completion: 1. Pass all badges 2. Pass any badge This doesn't provide the flexibility required. I've searched Moodle plug-ins and there doesn't appear to be a plug-in that supports such a format. Does anyone know of a way of achieving the above format?

ResponsesInList.Text: Unfortunately the answer is no. If you enable guest access to some course then any non logged in users can view all sections of your course. There is no option to grant guest access to any specific section of a course. Regards, Purnendu

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Guest access to course sections!
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello there. Yes this is possible but it requires some setting up. First - make your course guest access and put the items you want guests to see in a section on their own, say the top section for example. Then you will have to use the Restrict access settings of the other sections (or if you must, of individual items) to restrict access to people who have email addresses, You will see this as one of the possible options when setting restrict access. What happens is that guests who have not logged in will not be able to see the sections which are restricted to logged in users only, ie, those who have got an email address.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Courses on Demand and payment
ResponsesInList.Text: 1) Moodle has its own capability for dependency, so if you want a part/video to be watched before user can proceed to next level, one can do that yes, but this does not ascertain that the viewer has actually watched the video, so for example you have a video of 20 minutes, you can limit other sections to be opened if and only if that video section has been watched for 20 minutes, but then there is a catch, if user started the video and went off to make tea , I would take a small quiz right after video, based on that video to make sure the content has been watched. SCORM can do that yes, getting a quiz within a video, but SCORM support is bit shady, not that moodle doesn't supports it, but it sometimes has showed issues when upgrading to higher moodle versions. 2) for videos, Moodle can play videos directly when uploaded into courses, or linked from external source. but this will be Progressive Download only, means content will be downloaded into end user's PC then played (YouTube Embed is exception), therefore you dont need external server to play videos, BUT, if you want to stream videos (specifically thinking case of Adaptive BitRate Streams) where videos are played based on end-user bandwidth (low resolution videos for low bandwidth clients), then yes an external video streaming server with video player capable to handle that stream will be required, as well if you dont want users to download directly from your site using something like Internet download manager. As in case of ABR streaming, streaming server actually sends chunks of videos to end player rather than sending whole video. 3) Moodle is learning management system, BUT you can link to WordPress and use its capabilities (WooCommerce, Shopify etc Plug-ins) to get the shopping cart experience, where WordPress will work as the shopping front, listing all courses and moodle as actual course delivery/assessment mechanism. Now waiting for additional input from Mary, Helen, Emma, Ken, Rick etc as I am definitely below them in terms of suggestions.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Courses on Demand and payment
ResponsesInList.Text: A) When you mean adaptive Bitrate Streams is it a la Viemo ? (We want the videos to only be accessable if they paid for the course) B) Is Moodle unable to work as a front end system combined with.. lets say Enrolmart? I'm very new to making a platform and especially within ecommerce for E-learning. But from what I understand to make this happen I should do the following: 1) Buy a new webhost where Moodle can be integrated 2) Integrate Moodle into webhost, design frontend with or without wordpress. 3) Get an agreement with a gateway + Streaming site such as Vimeo 4)Make courses and have videos embedded into the courses 5) Integrate some sort of Shopping cart, which requires visitors to pay to get access to the courses + videos Would that be the "only" thing or am I being naive and missing some info now?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Courses on Demand and payment
ResponsesInList.Text: No, Vimeo doesn't sends adaptive streams (YouTube does however), you can however restrict videos to be viewed only by those who paid (there are multiple enrollment methods in moodle), so free users can't and paid users can access that specific modules holding videos. For front end as moodle, there has to be plug-in which I am not aware of any, if it's just video tutorials and simple quizzes, then you can as well give a thought to using WordPress as LMS and you'll have shopping cart available. Moodle is capable of doing plenty of things that most of the LMS's wont be able to, but if requirement is not that advanced, a simple solution would be more feasible. if you want to keep moodle as choice of implementation, then your steps are correct. however you can as well be able to find plenty of plug-ins in moodle, that are linked with streaming services.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Courses on Demand and payment
ResponsesInList.Text: That's not a big problem, I can tell you whole scenario and then you can choose which way to go. for preventing users to download the videos, you need to setup a streaming server, that will send the chunks of video rather than a whole down to client's player, this can be done either by using Apple's HLS or MPEG-DASH stream (DASH is a new entrant), so any capable media server that can serve both streams can be used - together with player that can support either streams. for streaming server, there are two options, one's Wowza streaming server, that will cost $65 a month plus additional hardware (dedicated server) to run it, and then there is Softvelum Nimble Streamer (my recommendation) that media server is free, you can optionally pay for the administration panel which costs $20 a month and supports 5 servers and is as well very light ( https://wmspanel.com/nimble )

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Course Upload is not restoring the course
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi everyone, I found the problem. The error message helped me to review the code and see where the process was stopping. It was failing on the execute_precheck function in the class restore_controller. The function checks/validates the source course before restoring. For some reason my source course had issues. To resolve it I created a blank course and import from the course with issues all the activities I wanted to be restored on the bulk course creation. So creating a blank course with the activities through the import gave me a good course to use to restore and create the other ones. Basically the issue was on the course that I was trying to restore from. Erika

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Collapsed Topics updated for Moodle 3.2 and 3.3....
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Rick, Thank you so much for your reply, video and insights. The 'Open / Close' all functionality has not gone!  You just need to edit the course settings and change 'One section' to 'No'.  That is because there is lots of new functionality in this release.  This new 'One section' setting when set to 'Yes' only allows one toggle section to be open at any one time on the 'main page' - it is separate to the clicking on the round icon to the single section page functionality.  That functionality removed the old confusing 'Course layout' setting which could be either one of 'Show all sections on one page' or 'One section per page' - now in effect both are combined. If when setting 'One section' to 'No' you still don't get 'Open / Close' all for a student then please let me know as its a bug! With the nav-draw problem I suspect that you've added the code in a given place such that the 'main page' with the toggles (the old 'Show all sections on one page' view with the toggles) does not have the link but the 'One section per page' (clinking on the new round icon) does.  So.... there could be a setting for this, but could be a quad state one of: Section links in nav-drawer. Section links in nav-drawer for 'main page' only. Section links in nav-drawer for 'single page' only. No section links in nav-drawer. Clearly the wording needs to be thought out.  What do you think? I hope that all makes sense. Cheers, Gareth

ResponsesInList.Text: Use backup and restore

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Duplicate course
ResponsesInList.Text: I do this all the time whenever I am getting ready for a new semester. Go to the course, then click on Backup.  Uncheck "Users" from what to copy.  Once Moodle backs up the course, I normally will download it to my computer.  Then I do a Restore, and at one point you can give it the Course Category, and a new name.  Restoring a course can take a little while, so be patient. Maybe I really don't need to save the backup to my computer, but this is probably what I do from my habits.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Duplicate course
ResponsesInList.Text: Of if you have several courses, way faster to do with the new upload courses feature where you can use your existing course as a template - I think that one feature has saved me a good two days worth of work every semester!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Duplicate course

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Duplicate course
ResponsesInList.Text: You don't create a template - the course itself is the template - that is the wonderful thing about it! You just create a csv file with your new course long name, short name, start date etc (follow documentation on that) and then have a template column where you reference the short name of the course that you want to copy.  Moodle then copies all the course content to your new courses in the background while you drink coffee.  I used to copy manually about 30 courses per semester and it took me at least a day's worth of work. Now I create one csv file, upload it to the course upload feature, and moodle does it all for me.  It is a truly beautiful thing - best feature to come out since I started!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Course Completion Issues
ResponsesInList.Text:
This isn't your quiz.  It IS the course completion settings.  I don't know why but sometimes the grade condition doesn't check.  It just prevents people from ever getting credit. One thing that sometimes helps:  Check your Grades.  If at the top of the screen it gives you a message that says, "Note: The aggregation method "Sum of grades" has been changed to "Natural" as
part of a site upgrade. Since "Sum of grades" was previously used in
this course, it is recommended that you review this change in the
gradebook.", you need to click okay.  Sometimes that will trigger the grade condition to actually function (not immediately, but on the sync cycle, you might have to reset completion, too).  Of course this means sometimes it won't. My general solution is to never use grade condition.  You've set a grade to pass on the quiz (green check), so it won't give them credit without passing.  The grade condition is just one more thing Moodle has to do to complete the course.  Try removing it and see what happens.

But does Moodle know what a passing grade for that quiz is?  Administration->Grades->Setup (tab), edit (on the quiz), edit settings, set the score needed to pass (not the percentage!).  You may have to click the Show more link...mine is a default show but I set it that way because instructors had such trouble finding it.  Then save.  Might solve the issue.  Also, if you require a passing gradein quiz settings, you must require a grade.  It seems redundant but won't work without it.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Course Completion Issues
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, Emily. Are you able to log in as the learner in question? If so, and I were trying to solve for this learner, I would look at the following things in this order: 1) If you are able to log in as this learner, first verify that the url resources are ticked off as complete on the front page from this learner's view. If not, then I would try to investigate why not. 2) Make sure you have set "grade to pass" in quiz settings as 8 and not 80, as Melanie said, and that your quiz points are set to be 10 and not 100 (all variables must match, here). 3) Check that you have set the completions requirements to be grade to pass + must receive grade (as Melanie said). 4) Check that your learner is posting a grade in the course total column and/or that there is not a conflict with number of attempts allowed/which attempt is marked as the one to post to the gradebook. 5) Not clear to me from your pic if you put in additional grade to pass for course requirement, so this is only relevant if you did: Review that your course total expectations for pass (if you have that set plus quiz) and your quiz total expectation for pass align (as in if you have 80 for course total, your course total column is set to be 100 and not 10). Sometimes the course total can be thrown off by the weighting in your gradebook categories and/or the course total requirement keeps the course completion from posting in cases where the course total is not posting for your learner in the grader report yet. If you check all of the above and still are not getting the expected results, perhaps post a pic of the completion settings area of the quiz so we can help you verify that the necessary variables are set there. Best, Lesli

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Course Completion Issues
ResponsesInList.Text:
Looking at the grade book: Do the students' grades on the quiz show up in green (or red)?  If they are black, the grade to pass has not been set.  If they are red, the grade to pass is set but incorrectly.  Green means passed, red means failed, black means no grade to pass set.  So, in the image below, we have a bunch of completed scorm modules (with no passing grade) and a few passed quizzes (green) which, like yours have 10 points (but my passing is 7) If the quiz grades appear in black, click the Setup tab at the top of
the grades page.  (By default, Grades opens on the tab circled in purple.  You click the tab in red ... Click Edit next to the quiz and choose Edit Settings. 
Find the grade to pass and set it.Setting the grade to pass looks like this (you may need to click a Show more): Looking in the Completion Status report:  Does a check for the quiz show up in completion at all?  If a grade shows up in the grade book as passed (green) and no check shows up in Status, your quiz settings may need another check. This is how your quiz settings should look to report completion properly. If all these things are set properly, you may have a cron issue?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Hidden sections -- view only, not control hide/show
ResponsesInList.Text: Yes -- absolutely possible. Sounds like you want your Inspector to have the ability to see the hidden sections of a course ( moodle/course:viewhiddensections ), but not control it's visibility ( moodle/course:sectionvisibility) - definitely two separate permissions. Another consideration -- add a folder to your course that has all the answer keys in it -- and either hide the folder (so students don't see it), group the folder to a specific group (such as a Teacher's Only group), or remove the students role's capability to 'view' this specific Folder (at the activity level).

ResponsesInList.Text: So are you looking for a 'video wall' kind of format, but where the videos are closed/collapsed until they are played? As far as I know there is no such format already available so that would have to be a custom build for you. Your best option for that is to hire a developer - unless you have the skills to do develop it yourself. Although, as Emma said, I'm not entirely sure that a course format is the best approach for this - it looks to me from your screenshot to be more of a Resource type than a course format that needs developing. Then each video is a single 'collapsed video' resource that expands to play when its button is clicked. On your other question - I'm also not aware of any plugin that enables mass uploading of resources, but anyway, they would need the context and course etc, so you really need to sort out the new developed resource or course format plugin first before you can look at how to then add your videos in bulk to your courses. I would guess that you need to add them all to some repository and then script them into the database - you'd probably need to upload one or two manually and investigate what changes there are to the database tables, where all the data is stored so that Moodle recognises the video files themselves, then use that investigation to write an sql script to write them into the database - possibly as URL links to wherever you store them.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Adding an Icon to Topics (section names)
ResponsesInList.Text: I did this with the Pioneer theme and you can use any fontawesome icon.  Just put in the code in the admin page. Here is a hint to help you - Use the :before CSS function. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Captivate project with no quiz
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello C Sand, Yeah, that SCORM resource is going to be specifically looking for a manifest file. Alternatively, you could upload your Captivate project as a file resource. Generic instructions for Moodle 2-3 1. In Captivate > Publish your Captivate project as a SWF and/or HTML5; ticking the box for Zip Files ; note the location of your published Zip file. 2. In Moodle > Add an activity or resource>Resources>File> navigate to your Zip file location>Upload your Zip file> once uploaded click the Zip file icon and select the 'Unzip button.' Once unzipped, you'll see all the individual files and folders included in your Captivate project. If you uploaded an HTML5 file, click on the index.html file. In the dialog box click 'Set main file' If you've uploaded a SWF, click on the .swf file. In the dialog box click 'Set main file' Save and return/display

ResponsesInList.Title: Fastest way to tidy a 'well loved' course with Backup & Restore?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi I hope this will be helpful to someone out there as I only recently realised the power of backup & restore for tidying up courses that have become full of old materials you no longer require. I had a course with 30 sections but only the first section was being used for current materials so I took a backup (default options) and restored into the same course with "Delete the contents of the existing course and then restore" with default options EXCEPT at step 4. Schema : Keep current roles and enrolments: YES Keep current groups and groupings: YES and I unchecked all items, then only selected those I wished to keep This left me with the same course, same enrolled users and their data but effectively deleted all the unwanted course materials. NB please do take care to keep your original course backup (and preferably have access to a recent full backup) because selecting the wrong options with 'delete & restore' can leave users unable to access your course or remove materials you wanted to keep! If in doubt, try restoring to a new course first and only over-write your existing course when you're happy you've done it right Carol

Hi Gareth, Sorry for all the trouble. My Moodle Partner (MP) figured out how to reset the image (see below) and that solved the problem. The only thing I can think of to solve this type of problem in the future is to have the image file reset to <brokenfile> or something so that if an image that was previously available for a particular section on the grid can no longer be found, it replaces with a placeholder image so that the code doesn't break and we can still access the Change Image link. Here's what the MP did to resolve the problem on my site: There is a trick we use when topic sections cannot be edited: we look at the URL id-number of the previous section in edit mode and then
alter the URL id-number - we replace it with a id-number greater or less than to get the non-editable section in edit mode. What we did specifically: In edit mode we clicked on" change image" for section 10 (last section functioning properly) and changed the URL sectionid from 205 to 204. We replaced the image and that corrected the broken layout. It took a bit of investigation - we had to look at which sectionids were available and which were missing. Example http:// mymoodlesite /course/format/grid/editimage.php? SECTIONID=205 &contextid=1584&userid=4&role=link&aria-label=Set%20or%20change%20image I hope this helps. Thanks for spending so much time helping me! Best wishes, Laura

```text
sections

     not the default English one by mistake so that the default value in the styles.
css
 file is used in preference.

CONTRIB-5817
.

URL
's when using single page display.

 12. Change 'Configuration' setting 'What to do with the toggles when the user first accesses the course, adds more sections or
     toggle peristence is off' to 'Initial toggle state' for clarity.
```
 M2.8: https://moodle.org/plugins/pluginversion.php?id=9226 
```text
  1. Fixed display of sections when 'Hidden sections' is set to 'Hidden sections are shown in collapsed form' and the
     'Structure' is one of 'Current topic first' or 'Current week first'.

  8. Fix missing ground signal icon in course settings 'Icon set' drop down.
```

 M2.9: https://moodle.org/plugins/pluginversion.php?id=9227 
```text
  1. Fixed display of sections when 'Hidden sections' is set to 'Hidden sections are shown in collapsed form' and the
     'Structure' is one of 'Current topic first' or 'Current week first'.
  2. Language files tidy up.
  3. Fix left and right section information not being displayed in Bootstrap V3 themes.
```

ResponsesInList.Title: Course - created by

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Course - created by
ResponsesInList.Text: This information is not stored directly in Moodle - you may be able to retrieve it from the logs. You haven't mentioned a Moodle version number, so I will assume you are using Moodle 2.9. The log event you are looking for is \core\event\course_created ( https://docs.moodle.org/dev/Event_2#Existing_events ). You will need to create an instance of \core\log\ sql _reader ( https://docs.moodle.org/dev/Migrating_log_access_in_reports ) and then use that to do a search for the relevant event. The 'userid' for that event will be the user who created the course.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Something between Weekly and Topics format

If you want to do this yourself, then have a look at: http://docs.moodle.org/dev/Course_Format and how the core and contributed formats are written. Cheers, Gareth

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Anchor tags
ResponsesInList.Text: Ok, I've looked into this - and did in the process discover a very minor logic flaw with CT - and I could react to 'section' and open up that section.  However, there seems to be no way of adding an anchor 'id' to the module that you want to link to. Delving deeper into the core code the course renderer '/course/renderer.php' has the method 'course_section_cm_name' which prints the name of the module.  That has a parameter '$displayoptions' which is an array, but nothing is done with it.  Ok, I believe that course formats cannot override this renderer, only themes, so that makes it tricky for CT by itself to implement a solution.  A theme could override the 'course_section_cm_name' method and add a generated id based upon some attribute of the 'cm_info' class that is passed in.  Then that would have the right combination of alterations to give a solution.  Pragmatically, if CT is to operate by itself and perhaps people want to do this in any course format or theme, then core code needs to be improved.  This would need a tracker issue (if there is not one already) to be processed in the normal way.  This means justifying the case, getting it voted upon by HQ and passed.  If passed, then as an enhancement the functionality would then go into M3.0.  If you wanted it back-ported, then a clear case would need to me made in a separate tracker issue, at least three weeks then need to pass after the original enhancement was integrated, then a decision would be made by HQ if the back-port was allowed.  If it was then separate branches need to be supplied and the normal tracker process followed.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: meta course: how to hide yet make accessible
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi everyone. Here's a possible way to make this work: 1. What you are calling a METACOURSE (M) does not need to be a metacourse. Take out the child courses. Take out all the users enrolled. Make this NOT a Metacourse, but make it Enrollable, Available to students and Allow guests without the key. (Administration > Settings > Is this a metacourse = No > Course enrollable = Yes > Availability = This course is available to students > Guest Access = Allow guests without the key) 2. Put the link to M inside Subcourse A and Subcourse B. 3. Put M inside some other SUBCATEGORY/SUBCATEGORIES that is/are not in the uppermost level. (This is assuming you have even got categories displayed on your home page at all. You can control how many levels of categories and sub-categories are displayed on the home page via Site Admin > Front Page > Front page settings > Maximum Category depth = 1) RESULT? 1. M is not displayed on the user's home page when they log in 2. The link to M is available in their Subcourse A and/or B 3. Clicking on the link to M displays content of M without enrolling the user into M (which of course would defeat your purpose again because then M would show up on their home page) 4. M is not in a top level category that is accessible to most users. It is buried deep somewhere in the bowels of your Moodle! Make sense? I'm eager to hear if this solves your puzzle! Good luck! Sarah

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: meta course: how to hide yet make accessible
ResponsesInList.Text: Using Moodle 1.9.8, here is a method to show only the meta course to the student and to not have the child courses listed via All Courses: Logged in with Administrator role: Create a Category for your child courses, e.g. Fall 2010 Child Courses , and place all the child courses in that category and hide the Fall 2010 Child Courses category. Add the instructor/professor/teacher to the teacher role of the child courses and hide the child courses [make unavailable to students] Create the meta course, add the child courses and set the instructor/professor/teacher in the teacher role of the meta course. Go to one of the child courses and copy the URL of the child course. In the meta course, add a resource of type Link to a file or web site , paste in the copied URL of the child course and then hide the added resource. Repeat steps 4 and 5 for each of the child courses that belong to the meta course. The reason we create the link to the child courses and set the instructor/professor/teacher to the teacher role of the child courses is to allow the teacher(s) to add/remove users from roles. If there is no need for the teachers to access the child courses, the creation of the links in the meta course is not needed.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: meta course: how to hide yet make accessible
ResponsesInList.Text: Greetings Jamal, Perhaps I am not understanding what your needs are so pardon me if I am on the wrong track here! Are your needs to have students from different courses share the same Moodle site? If so, then a metacourse is the site that the students interact with and not the "child" courses. To make the metacourse site visable to the students, we place the metacourse in the same category as their other courses - for example, Spring 2011 . The child courses - the course where the students are enrolled in and that are "connected" to the metacourse - are placed in another category that is a subcategory of Spring 2011 - for  example Spring 2011 Child Courses . The subcategory Spring 2011 Child Courses is hidden so the students and the professors do not see that category and the child courses listed. Then, in the metacourse at the top of the main page, we create links to each of the child courses and make those hidden so they do not show to the students but show to the professors. Since the professors are in the teacher role and the students are in the students role of the child courses, the professors and students can access the metacourse in their respective roles. Cheers!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Is it possible to add “make this the current topic” as a feature in “Restrict access”?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Gareth, Thanks for your encouraging response. I thought about your two questions. a) By what logic would I ensure that there is only ever one current topic? My suggestion: In case of conflict, make the topic with the lowest number current. So if topic 1 is the current topic, and topic 2 and 3 are set to open at the same date and time, applying the rule of the lowest number would make topic 2 the current topic. b) What happens when a user sets one manually? Make this topic current - now. Whether a user clicks on the light bulb or some code in "Restrict access" triggers the light bulb, both actions will only set the beginning of the current topic, but in my understanding they don't determine the method how the current topic is set. So a user could override this action any time later or just wait for the next "Restrict access" setting. Implementing "Make this topic current now" in "Restrict access" would eliminate one manual task for the teacher who uses the topics or collapsed topics format as well as improve the user experience as they would see consistently which topic is not only open and accessible, but also current. Thanks for all considerations. I readily admit that I have no clue how much work it is to implement such a feature. I just share my thoughts as I like to use MOODLE in online classes and face-to-face classes with online components. With kind regards, Hartmut

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Restrict groups on Enrolled Users
ResponsesInList.Text: I am presuming you want to limit the teacher to only seeing the users in their group.  You need to remove the permission Access All Groups.  This way they will only see or have access to the group that they are in. It is probably a good idea to create a new role for this purpose.  Just create a role based on the Teacher Role and then remove the permission.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Restrict groups on Enrolled Users

To do this for all teachers globally: Site administration>Users>Permissions>Define roles Select the editing teacher role; Click to edit the role Click the Show advanced button Type in the search box accessallgroups When it appears, click Prevent

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Hannah, Yes that's possible in Moodle 2.7 with plugin Group Choice installed (not yet released for Moodle 2.8) and using restrict access. Set up the groups in the course and name them for example Group A (Week 3+ 4) and Group B (Week 5-7). Add Group Choice as an activity in the week, where you want to give you students the choice, for example in week 2 and add these groups in Group Choice. Now you need to set the Restrict access conditions in the weeks, i.e., week 3 - restrict access to group A and close the eye (see screenshot below) so they will not see the access condition nor the activities of that particular week. They will still see the header of the weeks. Do this for all other weeks, for example for week 5, restrict access to Group B and close the eye. This worked for me in a Test course in Moodle 2.7. With kind regards, Hartmut

ResponsesInList.Title: screen readers and course formats and lists - oh my!
ResponsesInList.Text: If you're using a screen reader to view a moodle course you'll find something quite odd : Every label, activity or resource is indicated to be a separate list item. For a sighted user this isn't an issue - content on the screen appears to flow, just like on a normal website, with no indication its a bunch of separate items unless you're editing. For a screen reader user a label e.g. Course Reading - is separated from the resources/ activities it actually refers to There is no advantage to a screen reader of the course html list structure -  in testing with screen reader users it proved a barrier to navigation and understanding the course content structure, not an aid. For sighted user the underlying dom/html list structure is overwritten with css to not look like a list - which is just unnecessary code where more appropriate html elements are available. Historically i believe this all used to be tables in moodle, and was converted into lists at some point in the past, with css to make it not look like a list....? Moving forward we should probably just be using divs for label/resource/activity containers as most other websites do. These days we also have the article element - http://html5doctor.com/the-article-element/ - to group content that belongs together like a moodle section/topic or week. Anyway, just thought i'd post this here - interested to hear others thoughts/experiences around this strange choice of dom structure/html elements in moodle course formats.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: screen readers and course formats and lists - oh my!
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Stuart, If you believe that the code is wrong - change it.  Raise a tracker, submit the changes along with a test plan, get it peer reviewed.....and make a difference.  Nothing was ever achieved by moaning about it. There is no 'why'.  Moodle is old and decisions made in the past on how things were done are based upon the knowledge known at the time.  Things have moved on.  And when old code is recognised to be out of date then it needs to be improved for the very reasons the new knowledge justifies. Gareth

ResponsesInList.Text: Actually, what I have done is created a new Activity Module plugin that uses the code from Noticeboard to provide this functionality as an Activity that can be added to the top section of a course, regardless of the Course Format. We like the collapsible features of Flexible Sections -- we are currently using the Subpages module to provide a way to move chunks of activities and other content out of the regular flow of the course and into their own sections, but the functionality provided by Subpages is a bit clunky and really needs a change to Moodle Core, which Moodle HQ declines to make in favor of Flexible Sections. So what I would hope for is an expansion to Collapsed Topics/Weeks that would allow other collapsible subsections inside a section (topic or week). Then we would add our new  Module to provide display of the most recent (or most recent n) News posts.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Combine Noticeboard with Collapsed Topics or Collapsed Weeks?
ResponsesInList.Text: Interesting Elizabeth Pragmatically I do not like Flexible Sections (sorry Marina) because it is one of the few course formats that is destructive.  That is to say that if you decide later on to change the format of the course to another then you will find that the structure is all over the place.  Course formats should be non-destructive, like a 'view' in model - view - controller (MVC).  They are a presentation thing that should not affect the underlying structure of the data.  So if an educator at some point decides that a new course format is better then switching to that format should give the same section grouping of activities and resources.  It is for that reason that I will not introduce the Flexible Sections code into Collapsed Topics.

I had not realized (but should have realized) that Flexible Sections would cause the same problem. We won't want to use it, in that case. Collapsed Topics/Weeks goes a long way toward solving the "scroll of death" problem, but I can still see a case for grouping several Activities and Resources together in some way that allows them to be shown or hidden by the user. What other method of doing this might work in Moodle? Could some kind of CSS method be used to give the user a way to collapse indented content, like the Tree display in the sidebar menus? I think that would be relatively intuitive for users, if it could be done. It would be great if it could be part of a Course Format, rather than part of a Theme.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Collapsed Topics - Open or Closed when returning to a page
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Richard, If you look in: Home-> Site administration -> Plugins -> Course formats -> Collapsed Topics - you will find a setting 'defaulttogglepersistence' to turn of the functionality that remembers the state of the toggles. By default, you set the course date and everyone follows along with the course schedule. Everyone enrolled in this system must start at the same time, and upon completion, end at the same time. What if people need to be able to start at different times? Can you set up individualized start times for the same course? To be clear, let's say we have a 10-week course. There are 100 users that need to be enrolled. But they cannot all start on the same date. Do you have to create a course for each start date? I hope my question is clear and thanks for your help.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Personalized course start times
ResponsesInList.Text: Interesting that this same question has come up a couple of times now.  The quick answer is no, afaik, you cannot assign different start and end times for a course.... However, if you get away from the time idea, you can set completion settings on the course and then start groups of students separating them out with groups and using completion and restrictions to push them through the content in the correct order..

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Personalized course start times
ResponsesInList.Text: We do individually-paced math courses in Moodle. Students are added and removed daily. We even allow students to postpone. We do not set dates on the course start. We have groups, as Emma mentioned. Students are added to the groups to maintain about even numbers. Our registration system (separate from Moodle) calculates when a student's term is done. We use a csv file once a day to upload new students and remove students whose time has run out. Technically, we use suspend both for postponements and and end of term. Suspend preserves the students' data but prevents them from doing any work in the course. Since these are individually-paced courses, there is no schedule to follow. Students can do as much math as they can stand in a 3-month period.

ResponsesInList.Title: Only view one topic when editing a course?
ResponsesInList.Text: Is there any way to, as a teacher, only view one topic of a course when in editing mode? I reuse courses from one year to the next, so there are a LOT of activities in the course. Even thought the course is set to show one topic only, when I enter editing mode, it displays all the topics, which makes the page take quite a while to load, since there are many activities. This means doing simple administrative things on the course (adding assignments, editing multiple assignments, etc.) takes a lot longer since each time it must reload the page, it must load the entire course. It seems this is the standard behavior, but I was hoping someone with more experience than me might have a good solution? (One alternative would be if there is an easy way to copy an entire topic from one course to another. Then I can just copy topics of the course as the year progresses). Thanks so much.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Only view one topic when editing a course?
ResponsesInList.Text: Have you thought about using Metacourse 's to break up the course into smaller more manageable chunks?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Only view one topic when editing a course?
ResponsesInList.Text: I hadn't thought of metacourses; I'm not too familiar with them. My understanding was they exist to allow multiple courses to share resources. That's not really what I want to do here. I have one course that just happens to already have a year's worth of resources in it, so the course page is very long when all topics are displayed on the same page. Am I misunderstanding metacourses? Thanks.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Only view one topic when editing a course?
ResponsesInList.Text: Metacourses allow one course to be 'master' course that you enrol on.  Then you have child courses that can be accessed without further enrolment.  Therefore you can break down a large course into manageable sections .  Each course has its own set of contained activities / resources.  You would need to backup / restore the big course into each of the child courses and remove the activities / resources you know longer need.  Big job. An alternative is a programmatic one such that when editing you have to click on a section to edit them as you want.  However, this means that moving activities / resources between sections is impossible.  This does mean modifying the code.  It would be possible, but how long to work out the changes, difficult to say without a de-risking exercise. Or use Collapsed Topics where all of the activities / resources are still there, just not shown unless you open a toggle.  Therefore easier to D&D from say section 30 to section 1.  Page load probably the same as you currently have. Critically I would start to question why a course has become so big.  Perhaps consider leaving it as is and then progressively transfer to a metacourse solution with a course for each section.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Gif animation file in the grid format didn"t show the animation
ResponsesInList.Text: Ok, a quick test on Moodle 2.6.1 and my latest unreleased development version 2014011400 shows that I can replicate the problem.  However, the format uses the PHP GD library to resize the uploaded images which currently does not support reading of animated Gif's - http://www.php.net/manual/en/function.imagecreatefromgif.php .  There is a link to another library - http://www.gdenhancer.com/ - which claims to support them.  However it is for PHP 5.4 and only M2.7 is proposed to have PHP 5.4 as a minimum requirement.  Thus cannot be the solution in M2.5 or M2.6.  Additionally I don't know at this moment in time how difficult it would be to use the library or indeed might make the installation process difficult. Therefore at this moment in time, there is nothing I can do to solve the problem.  Sorry. Cheers, Gareth

Imagemagick instead of GD, supports animated gifs (at least according to wikipedia), but is a seperate php extension to be installed. 2. Offer direct uploads without processing the files through GD. In our training environment--and I'm sure other environments are like this as well--multiple users have 'developer' access to a specific course: A small group of instructional designers will have developer access to all courses. We want to move to 2.6.3. (Also, we can't go above 2.6.3 right now because we're limited by the PHP version on our servers. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Add Course - Shows system password in course field!
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Jean, I'm using Moodle 2.6.3+ (Build: 20140613) and could not replicate: How did you install?  Was some old code left about if you upgraded a test system?  Could you try one of the standalone packages and see if it happens there for you, from the top of: http://download.moodle.org/ Cheers, Gareth

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Add Course - Shows system password in course field!
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks, Gareth. Actually when you mentioned 'old code' it reminded me of how some browsers use 'auto fill'--and when we just went back through here, that's where we found the problem. I found that if you're using a browser like Chrome and you have auto-fil turned on, you can end up with the issue that I indicated above. Since we have quite a few people with the Developer Role and we never use the 'Guest Access' function, and I didn't want to worry about a variety of browser setups, I just turned OFF the 'Assign Roles' permission for the Developer Role. The section will only move if you can drag it past the half-way point of the section above, and if that section is long then it can't be done (the page doesn't scroll when you drag to the top of the window). Is there any other way to reorder sections apart from drag and drop? Apart, that is, from turning off Javascript altogether (not practical on a production site)? Apologies if this has been asked before, I couldn't find it! Thanks Steve

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moving long sections
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Steve, You are talking about the 'Frontpage'?  If so then you could turn off JavaScript at the browser end in its settings and then the arrows would appear. Cheers, Gareth

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moving long sections
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Gareth, I meant the course homepage. But yes, that would work, good idea. It's still not ideal though - perhaps even a bug? If you can't move sections in a course the normal way, there ought to be a way to do it without having to reconfigure your browser. Thanks! Steve

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moving long sections
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Steve, Indeed.  However as its the course page, then you could install my Collapsed Topics format ( https://moodle.org/plugins/view.php?plugin=format_topcoll ) and be able to move whole collapsed sections with their content without seeing their content.  The format is non-destructive so can be changed to and from other formats (ones that are equally non-destructive) without damage. Cheers, Gareth

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moving long sections
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Gareth, That's also a good idea, and we are looking at installing that anyway, so that's perfect. Thanks for all your help! Steve

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moving long sections
ResponsesInList.Text:
Don't use drag and drop. Just click on the 'move' icon, a

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Word wrap not working on Collapsed Topics
ResponsesInList.Text: Gareth, I looked at your suggested code in your styles.css, and I think that I discovered that you might be using some incorrect arguments for these CSS styles. word-break: break-word; overflow-wrap: break-word; word-wrap: break-word; You were able to cause me to explore these CSS properties, and I discovered the correct arguments and came upon a solution that works in Safari, Chrome, IE11, Firefox, and Safari on my iPhone .  I put this code in the CSS box of MORE (2.7), and it worked.  I am not sure if you would want to integrate these changes in CT styles.css.  By the way, apparently word-wrap might now be superseded by overflow-wrap, so having both in here might be redundant.  I am not sure about this, so I am including both. .course-content ul.ctopics li.section .content .toggle a  h3, .course-content ul.ctopics li.section .content.sectionhidden h3  { word-wrap: normal; overflow-wrap: normal; word-break: normal; }

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Word wrap not working on Collapsed Topics
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Rick, I decided on 'break-word' because it seemed to be more appropriate in testing: http://www.w3schools.com/cssref/css3_pr_word-wrap.asp . overflow-wrap has indeed superseded word-wrap, but not all browsers support it which is why it is there: http://caniuse.com/#search=overflow-wrap Cheers, Gareth

ResponsesInList.Title: Drag & drop reordering
ResponsesInList.Text: Right here's a question I have a 2 semester course format, it is inherits from the topics course format, and the *only* difference is that it presents the sections under 2 tabs: Semester 1 and Semester 2. Without any additional modifications (really) drag and drop works nicely for uploading and reordering *resources*, but it doesn't work for re-ordering sections. I've implemented this by setting section 0 to be always displayed but each subsequent section is semester 1 or semester 2 based on if it is an odd or even section (by doing $section % 2) Section 1: Semester 2 Section 2: Semester 1 My renderer then simply does a "continue" on each section that doesn't satisfy this condition. Now it would appear that the section re-ordering works on the basis of knowing the section being dragged (by it's "id", which apparently is actually it's ordinal position) and the "position" of the destination section that its being dropped on to. This is obviously not going to work in this case, because I'm not actually simply moving items up or down, I'm needing to reorder them within the odd or event items of the whole list. I have a nice piece of PHP that does this perfectly *if* you're not using Javascript (ie the up/down buttons) which is easy to hooking as the renderer for the up/down icons simply points at this script instead of the default one. How do I get the Drag & drop to have different logic? Or equally how can I disable *only* the drag & drop section re-ordering (so I get the "static" reorder controls) but keep the d&d upload & resource reordering.. Oh and how can I do this from within the course format only, and *without* hacking the core.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Drag & drop reordering
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Michael, The starting point for your investigations is the 'format.js' file contained in the course format's folder.  It has functions that are concerned with initialisation and drag and drop.  But unlike PHP, you will need to perform a 'Purge all caches' every time you make a change to see the effect. I currently do not know how to disable JS D&D in an individual course format. Cheers, Gareth

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Drag & drop reordering
ResponsesInList.Text: This doesn't appear to help me. It actually appears to work on the Javascript side, with the nodes simply swapping places in the DOM, however the re-ordering actually breaks and I think there may be a problem in the "core". So... I'm simply extending the topics format, but skipping every 2nd (ignoring the "general" topic 0 section) section. If I have Pos 0: [Section-0]* Pos 1: [Section-1]* Pos 2: [Section-2] Pos 3: [Section-3]* Pos 4: [Section-4] Pos 5: [Section-5]* Items marked * are being displayed and I want to move section 5 to section 3 (Pos 5 -> pos 3). Pos 0: [Section-0]* Pos 1: [Section-1]* Pos 2: [Section-2] Pos 3: [Section-5]* Pos 4: [Section-3]* Pos 5: [Section-4] However note this shifts the section-3 down one place into pos 4, so I also need to move section-3 from pos-3 in to pos-5, to prevent things get screwed up: Pos 0: [Section-0]* Pos 1: [Section-1]* Pos 2: [Section-2] Pos 3: [Section-5]* Pos 4: [Section-4] Pos 5: [Section-3]* I can't find a way to hook in to anywhere to override the re-ordering. The move_section_to() function in course/lib.php defines the move action, which makes it impossible for a course format to define it's own custom section moving logic. The call to course_get_format($course)->ajax_section_move() is insufficient as it executes *after* the (incorrect) move operations take place. I would have thought it made more sense for move_section_to() to be implemented against format_base and overridden as appropriate by the course format.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Drag & drop reordering
ResponsesInList.Text: Dear Michael, Ok, the PHP orders the page as you have done in the 'renderer.php' of the course format.  With JavaScript on, 'format.js' in the format gets called with the 'from' and 'to' identifiers for what has been moved on the page.  IT does the reordering at the client side and then uses AJAX to tell the server what it has done.  Therefore you need to debug and understand the nature of that JavaScript in order to see what data is available to it so it can therefore make a suitable decision and order the DOM nodes accordingly.  You may need to add extra attributes in order to accomplish this task.  And check that the AJAX update data is correct. Or it might be a case that you should not output the intermittent sections at all in the PHP. Gareth

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Course Structure
ResponsesInList.Text: I think you will find Moodle to be very flexible, with many ways to accomplish your goals.  When I read your question, it makes me think "Hmmm, this person is coming from a Blackboard environment". I am not one who can describe the many ways to structure Moodle, but I can tell you what I do. Moodle can organize a course by topic, what you call "subject".  Then, all of the materials needed for that topic can be put into this topic.  You can create a folder, if you wish, that might contain even more resources.  It's as simple as that.  In this way, students can easily see all of the topics and select the one that they are interested in.  The instructor can also "highlight" the current topic, which is what I do. I like the add-in "Collapsed Topics" so that one can "collapse" completed topics. If anything that I say is of interest to you, you are welcome to watch some of my videos that I give to students that show them how my course is using Moodle.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Missing settings in Collapsed Topics
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Matt, Ok, I think after a few hours investigation that I have a solution where an installation of Collapsed Topics has gone wrong and the capabilities have not been created.  Therefore please try the following procedure (everybody else DO NOT try on a production server until confirmed as ok, and even then after a backup): Put Moodle in maintenance mode. Assuming that CT files are already in place in '/course/format/topcoll'. Remove all 'topcoll' ('format_topcoll' and 'format/topcoll') rows from the following tables in the database: config_plugins, capabilities, role_capabilities and course_format_options. In the 'config' table, find the row for 'allversionshash' ('name' attribute) and set to an empty string, i.e. clear completely. Perform a 'Purge all caches'. Go to 'Site administration -> Notifications'.  The URL should have no 'cache' parameter and if it does, change to 'cache=0' and reload. This should kick start the update checking mechanism and reinstall the format. Put Moodle out of maintenance mode. Note: If you had set any previous CT specific course settings, then these will be lost. Cheers, Gareth

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: The great Collapsed Topics arrow debate.
ResponsesInList.Text: Mary, I like your thinking about the language.  If the arrow was showing the "state", then the word should be changed from "Open" to "Opened", likewise for "Closed". If we think about the use of the "+" and "-" symbols used in Moodle's blocks, the "+" symbol is shown when you want to "Open" a block.  Once opened, the "-" symbol is shown.  So block symbols are using the "verb" form (i.e., if you want to open a block, click on the "+" symbol, if you then want to close a block, click on the "-" symbol.  This is why I think that the arrows in Gareth's heading should be changed. It is no problem for anyone to make these match their own idea (by changing code or pictures in the plug-in, but I think that Gareth wants to really get it correct (whatever that means). Thanks for your thoughts.

Therefore with those time and version constraints you are better off requesting / working with the developers of the block manager ( https://moodle.org/plugins/view.php?plugin=block_cmanager ) to iron out the bugs and add in the features you require.  I had a quick look at the code and there is a separate database table where new options have already been added.  And block do support storage of files - http://docs.moodle.org/dev/File_API#File_areas - however, I do know from the grid format that file upload and storage is not simple.  Despite all of this, the contributed solution will be the fastest option, even if you fork the code and perform the work yourself.  The source code is after all GPLv3 as with all code and plugins in Moodle, so you can copy and improve on it.
